1	---
2	
3	description: "Task list for the No Overlapping Bookings feature"
4	---
5	
6	# Tasks: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room
7	
8	**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/`
9	
10	**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md
11	
12	**Tests**: Included. FR-024 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: a spec task marked "failing" is done first and MUST fail (a compile error on a missing export counts) before the implementation task that follows it.
13	
14	**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.
15	
16	## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`
17	
18	- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
19	- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
20	- Every task names the exact file it creates, edits or runs
21	
22	## Path Conventions
23	
24	Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/contract/src/lib/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/web/src/views/bookings/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.
25	
26	## Rules that apply to every task
27	
28	- The only change to `libs/contract` is T002 (FR-015). Nothing is changed in `apps/room`, `apps/gateway`, `apps/worker`, `libs/backend-common`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `apps/web/src/services`, `package.json` or `specs/001-room-bookings` (FR-021, FR-022). No table, migration, route, message pattern or dependency is added.
29	- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value from `@roombook/contract`.
30	- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method and query function, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
31	- Transactions only in repositories. `.env` files are never read; configuration is referred to by variable name. Git stays local.
32	
33	## Assumptions made in this task list
34	
35	1. **Spec files and the 200-line limit.** plan.md lists the existing specs as "edit", but four of them are within 25 lines of the limit. New cases therefore go to a new sibling file where the existing one would pass 200 lines: `idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts`, `booking.repository.update.spec.ts`, `booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx` and `bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx`. `create-booking.service.spec.ts`, `booking.service.spec.ts` and `booking-edit-dialog.spec.tsx` are edited in place; if one of them would reach 200 lines, its new cases move to a sibling `<name>.overlap.spec.ts(x)` instead.
36	2. **Names the design leaves open.** The two query functions are `lockRoom` and `isRoomSpanTaken`; the error function is `raiseBookingOverlap`; the new repository method is `BookingRepository.update`; the update result holds a `BookingEntity | null`.
37	3. **Repository specs mock `./booking-overlap.query`** with `jest.mock`, so the SQL text of the lock and the check is asserted once, in `booking-overlap.query.spec.ts`.
38	4. **User Story 3 adds no code.** The room lock is part of the create and update transactions built in User Stories 1 and 2 (plan.md, research R1); taking it out of them to add it later would leave those stories half-built. The unit tests that pin the lock and the order of statements are in those stories; the User Story 3 phase is the proof of the race against the running stack (research R7).
39	5. **User Story 4 specs are expected to pass when first run** (research R6): the page already has the behaviour. They are regression tests for the new error; a component is edited only if one of them fails.
40	6. `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `update-booking-result.dto.ts` hold no logic and get no spec of their own (plan.md).
41	7. T008 and T014 change existing specs so they keep passing with the new collaborators; they are not failing-first tasks.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)
46	
47	**Purpose**: Confirm the starting point; the project, tooling and dependencies already exist.
48	
49	- [ ] T001 Run `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` from the repository root (scripts in `package.json`) and confirm all three pass before any change; stop and report if one fails
50	
51	---
52	
53	## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)
54	
55	**Purpose**: The one contract change and the two shared pieces both write paths use: the room lock with the overlap check, and the overlap rejection.
56	
57	**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.
58	
59	- [ ] T002 Edit `libs/contract/src/lib/error-code.enum.ts`: add the member `BOOKING_OVERLAP = 'CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP'` on the line after `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`; change nothing else in `libs/contract`
60	- [ ] T003 [P] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.query.spec.ts` with an `EntityManager` whose `query` is a `jest.fn()`: `lockRoom(manager, roomId)` runs exactly one statement, `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0))`, with the parameters `['room:<roomId>']`, and two different room ids give two different lock names; `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, roomId, startsAt, endsAt, excludedBookingId)` runs exactly one statement whose text contains `"room_id" = $1`, `"starts_at" < $3`, `"ends_at" > $2` and `$4::uuid IS NULL OR "id" <> $4::uuid` and does not contain `confirmation_status`, with the parameters `[roomId, startsAt, endsAt, excludedBookingId]` (`null` passed through as `null`), and returns `true` for the row `[{ taken: true }]` and `false` for `[{ taken: false }]`
61	- [ ] T004 [P] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.error.spec.ts` (after T002): `raiseBookingOverlap()` throws an `RpcException` whose error is exactly `{ statusCode: 409, errorCode: ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP, message: 'The room is already booked for that time' }` (read the error the way the `errorOf` helper of `create-booking.service.spec.ts` does)
62	- [ ] T005 [P] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.query.ts` exporting `lockRoom(manager: EntityManager, roomId: string): Promise<void>` (kind: transaction-scoped advisory lock, waiting (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`); name: `room:<roomId>`, hashed with `hashtextextended(…, 0)`) and `isRoomSpanTaken(manager: EntityManager, roomId: string, startsAt: Date, endsAt: Date, excludedBookingId: string | null): Promise<boolean>` (`SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "bookings" WHERE "room_id" = $1 AND "starts_at" < $3 AND "ends_at" > $2 AND ($4::uuid IS NULL OR "id" <> $4::uuid)) AS "taken"`): a stored booking `b` is in the way when `b.room_id = R AND b.starts_at < end AND b.ends_at > start`, and, on update, `b.id` is not the booking being changed; both are plain functions, not providers (T003 passes)
63	- [ ] T006 [P] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.error.ts` exporting `raiseBookingOverlap(): never`, one statement: `ExceptionHelper.conflict(ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP, 'The room is already booked for that time')` (T004 passes; depends on T002)
64	
65	**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run test` pass; user story work can begin.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## Phase 3: User Story 1 - A room cannot be double-booked on create (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP
70	
71	**Goal**: `POST /api/bookings` for a span that overlaps a booking of the same room is answered 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; nothing is stored against the booking, the `Idempotency-Key` or the queue. Touching spans and other rooms are still accepted.
72	
73	**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create a booking for a room, then send creates for the same room that overlap it, touch it and sit in another room, and reuse the key of a rejected create (quickstart scenarios 1, 2 and 3).
74	
75	### Tests for User Story 1 (write first, must fail) ⚠️
76	
77	- [ ] T007 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts` with the `DataSource`, query runner and `manager` mocked as in `idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts` and `./booking-overlap.query` mocked with `jest.mock`: (a) free span — `claim` calls `lockRoom(manager, booking.roomId)` then `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, booking.roomId, new Date(booking.startsAt), new Date(booking.endsAt), null)`, in this order by `invocationCallOrder`: `manager.findOneBy` (stored key) → `lockRoom` → `isRoomSpanTaken` → `manager.save`, and answers `CREATED`; (b) `isRoomSpanTaken` resolves `true` — the result is `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }`, `manager.save` and `manager.insert` are not called, the transaction is committed once, not rolled back, and the runner released once; (c) for each of `IN_PROGRESS` (first try-lock not obtained), `KEY_REUSED` (second try-lock not obtained), `REPLAYED` (stored row, same fingerprint) and `KEY_REUSED` (stored row, other fingerprint) neither `lockRoom` nor `isRoomSpanTaken` is called
78	- [ ] T008 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts`: add `jest.mock('./booking-overlap.query')` and, in `beforeEach`, make `isRoomSpanTaken` resolve `false` and `lockRoom` resolve; change no existing case and keep the file under 200 lines
79	- [ ] T009 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.spec.ts`: in `claim outcomes` add a failing case — a claim `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }` raises 409 with `errorCode` `ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and the message `The room is already booked for that time`, and `ConfirmationQueueProducer.enqueue` is not called; in `the same key after a rejected request` add a failing case — after an `OVERLAP` claim, the same key and body with the claim still `OVERLAP` raises the same 409 again (not a replay), and the same key with a claim that answers `CREATED` returns `{ booking, replayed: false }` and enqueues exactly one job
80	
81	### Implementation for User Story 1
82	
83	- [ ] T010 [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/claim-booking-result.dto.ts`: add `OVERLAP = 'OVERLAP'` to `ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum` after `IN_PROGRESS`
84	- [ ] T011 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.ts`: in `claimWithin`, after the stored-key branch and before `insertBookingWithKey`, call `lockRoom(manager, booking.roomId)`, then `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, booking.roomId, new Date(booking.startsAt), new Date(booking.endsAt), null)`, and return `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }` when it is `true`; the order inside the transaction is: try-lock key+fingerprint → try-lock key → read stored key → lock room (waits) → overlap check → insert booking + idempotency row (T007 passes, T008 stays green; depends on T005, T010)
85	- [ ] T012 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.ts`: in `toResult`, after the `IN_PROGRESS` branch, call `raiseBookingOverlap()` when the outcome is `ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP`; the enqueue stays limited to outcome `CREATED` and the order of the earlier checks (stored key, time pair, room) is not changed (T009 passes; depends on T006, T010)
86	
87	**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run test` passes; quickstart scenarios 1, 2 and 3 pass against the running stack.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Phase 4: User Story 2 - A room cannot be double-booked by moving a booking (Priority: P2)
92	
93	**Goal**: `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` whose resulting span overlaps another booking of the same room is answered 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and leaves the booking unchanged; 404 and 400 are answered as before and win over overlap; a booking never conflicts with itself.
94	
95	**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create two bookings of one room that do not overlap, then update one with times that overlap the other, touch the other and stay within its own span (quickstart scenario 4).
96	
97	### Tests for User Story 2 (write first, must fail) ⚠️
98	
99	- [ ] T013 [P] [US2] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.update.spec.ts` for `BookingRepository.update(id, changes)`, with the `BookingEntity` repository token mocked, the `DataSource` mocked as a query runner whose `manager` has `findOneBy` and `query` (pattern of `idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts`), and `./booking-overlap.query` mocked; the stored booking is 09:00–10:00 in room `R`: (a) first read finds no row → `{ outcome: NOT_FOUND, booking: null }`, `lockRoom` not called; (b) the read after the lock finds no row → `NOT_FOUND`; (c) `{ endsAt: 09:00 }` and `{ startsAt: 10:30 }` → `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` (resulting `ends_at` not later than resulting `starts_at`; the stored value is used for the time that was not sent), `isRoomSpanTaken` not called; (d) `isRoomSpanTaken` resolves `true` → `OVERLAP` with `booking: null` and no `UPDATE`; (e) `{ endsAt: 11:00 }` → `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, R, stored start, 11:00, id)` and one `UPDATE "bookings"` whose text still contains `"title" = COALESCE($2::varchar, "title")`, `"starts_at" = COALESCE($3::timestamptz, "starts_at")`, `"ends_at" = COALESCE($4::timestamptz, "ends_at")`, `"updated_at" = now()`, `COALESCE($4::timestamptz, "ends_at") > COALESCE($3::timestamptz, "starts_at")` and `RETURNING`, with the parameters `[id, null, null, new Date(11:00)]`, answering `{ outcome: UPDATED, booking: <returned row> }`; (f) a title-only change takes the lock and checks the stored span; (g) the `UPDATE` returns no row → `NOT_FOUND`; (h) order by `invocationCallOrder`: first read → `lockRoom(manager, R)` → second read → `isRoomSpanTaken` → `UPDATE`; (i) every outcome commits once and releases once; a statement that rejects rolls back, releases and rethrows
100	- [ ] T014 [P] [US2] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.spec.ts`: remove the `updateIfTimeRangeValid` describe (its SQL assertions now live in T013) and add `{ provide: DataSource, useValue: { createQueryRunner: jest.fn() } }` to the providers; change no other case
101	- [ ] T015 [P] [US2] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.service.spec.ts`: mock `BookingRepository.update` in place of `updateIfTimeRangeValid` and replace the three cases that follow the repository update with four failing ones — `UPDATED` returns the mapped DTO; `NOT_FOUND` raises 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` (`Booking not found`); `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` raises 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` (`endsAt must be later than startsAt`); `OVERLAP` raises 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` (`The room is already booked for that time`) — and in all four `findById` is not called; the no-field case (stored booking returned, `update` not called) and the unparsable-time case (400, `update` not called) stay as they are
102	
103	### Implementation for User Story 2
104	
105	- [ ] T016 [US2] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/update-booking-result.dto.ts` exporting `enum UpdateBookingOutcomeEnum { UPDATED, NOT_FOUND, INVALID_TIME_RANGE, OVERLAP }` (string values equal to the names) and `class UpdateBookingResultDto { outcome: UpdateBookingOutcomeEnum; booking: BookingEntity | null }`
106	- [ ] T017 [P] [US2] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.ts`: inject `DataSource`, delete `updateIfTimeRangeValid` and add `update(id: string, changes: UpdateBookingDto): Promise<UpdateBookingResultDto>` as one query-runner transaction (commit, rollback on error, release — the shape of `IdempotentBookingRepository.claim`): 1. read the booking by id with the transaction's manager — no row → `NOT_FOUND`; 2. `lockRoom(manager, roomId)`; 3. read the booking again — no row → `NOT_FOUND`; 4. form the resulting span from the sent times and the stored ones — end not later than start (`isEndAfterStart`) → `INVALID_TIME_RANGE`; 5. `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, roomId, start, end, id)` → `OVERLAP`; 6. run the existing conditional `UPDATE … RETURNING` statement unchanged on the manager → `UPDATED` with the row, or `NOT_FOUND` when it returns no row; every rejecting outcome returns before step 6; `deleteById`, `findPage`, `findById` and `recordConfirmationResult` are not changed and take no lock; the file stays under 200 lines (T013 passes, T014 stays green; depends on T005, T016)
107	- [ ] T018 [P] [US2] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.service.ts`: `updateBooking` keeps its two earlier checks (no field → `findBookingById`; a time that does not parse → 400), then calls `bookingRepository.update(id, changes)` and maps the outcome — `UPDATED` → `toBookingDto(result.booking)`, `NOT_FOUND` → 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` `Booking not found`, `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` → 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` `endsAt must be later than startsAt`, `OVERLAP` → `raiseBookingOverlap()`; remove the follow-up `findBookingById` read that told 404 from 400 (T015 passes; depends on T006, T016)
108	
109	**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run test` passes; quickstart scenario 4 passes against the running stack; scenarios 1 to 3 still pass.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## Phase 5: User Story 3 - Two people cannot take the same room at the same moment (Priority: P3)
114	
115	**Goal**: Two overlapping creates for one room arriving together end as exactly one 201 and one 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, with one booking, one confirmation job and one stored idempotent response; the same holds for an update racing with a create.
116	
117	**Independent Test**: Send two overlapping creates for the same room at the same moment, each with its own `Idempotency-Key`, 100 times; after every round count the answers and the stored bookings (quickstart scenario 5).
118	
119	**No code in this phase** (assumption 4): the lock was built and unit-tested in T003, T005, T007, T011, T013 and T017. These tasks prove it against the running stack. They need the gateway port by name, `GATEWAY_PORT`; if it is not set in the shell, do not read a `.env` file — report the task as not run and ask the owner. If a round gives another result, stop, report the output and do not weaken the expectation; the fix belongs in `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.ts` or `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.ts`, test first.
120	
121	- [ ] T019 [US3] After `pnpm run stack:reset`, run the 100-round loop of scenario 5 in `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/quickstart.md` and confirm its output is the single line `100 201 409`; then confirm the checks of its table: 100 bookings for the room, every one `SENT` with 1 attempt 10 seconds later, and no job in `tmp/logs/worker.log` for a booking that does not exist (SC-003, SC-004)
122	- [ ] T020 [US3] Run the three variations of scenario 5 in `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/quickstart.md`, a few rounds each: room R and room S with the same span → `201 201`; room R 10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00 → `201 201`; the same key and body twice → one booking, and never `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` (FR-014)
123	- [ ] T021 [US3] Run scenario 6 of `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/quickstart.md` about 20 times (needs User Story 2): a `PATCH` that extends booking A to 11:30 racing with a create for 11:00–12:00 in the same room → every round exactly one of the two succeeds, the other is 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, and the room's bookings never overlap (FR-013)
124	
125	**Checkpoint**: SC-003 is met; the outputs of T019 to T021 are reported.
126	
127	---
128	
129	## Phase 6: User Story 4 - See the conflict on the Bookings page without losing the input (Priority: P4)
130	
131	**Goal**: On `/bookings`, an overlap rejection of a create or an edit shows the API's `message` inside the form that was submitted, keeps everything typed, and disappears after the next successful submit.
132

# Tasks: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md

**Tests**: Included. FR-024 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: a spec task marked "failing" is done first and MUST fail (a compile error on a missing export counts) before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates, edits or runs

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/contract/src/lib/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/web/src/views/bookings/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- The only change to `libs/contract` is T002 (FR-015). Nothing is changed in `apps/room`, `apps/gateway`, `apps/worker`, `libs/backend-common`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `apps/web/src/services`, `package.json` or `specs/001-room-bookings` (FR-021, FR-022). No table, migration, route, message pattern or dependency is added.
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value from `@roombook/contract`.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method and query function, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. `.env` files are never read; configuration is referred to by variable name. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. **Spec files and the 200-line limit.** plan.md lists the existing specs as "edit", but four of them are within 25 lines of the limit. New cases therefore go to a new sibling file where the existing one would pass 200 lines: `idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts`, `booking.repository.update.spec.ts`, `booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx` and `bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx`. `create-booking.service.spec.ts`, `booking.service.spec.ts` and `booking-edit-dialog.spec.tsx` are edited in place; if one of them would reach 200 lines, its new cases move to a sibling `<name>.overlap.spec.ts(x)` instead.
2. **Names the design leaves open.** The two query functions are `lockRoom` and `isRoomSpanTaken`; the error function is `raiseBookingOverlap`; the new repository method is `BookingRepository.update`; the update result holds a `BookingEntity | null`.
3. **Repository specs mock `./booking-overlap.query`** with `jest.mock`, so the SQL text of the lock and the check is asserted once, in `booking-overlap.query.spec.ts`.
4. **User Story 3 adds no code.** The room lock is part of the create and update transactions built in User Stories 1 and 2 (plan.md, research R1); taking it out of them to add it later would leave those stories half-built. The unit tests that pin the lock and the order of statements are in those stories; the User Story 3 phase is the proof of the race against the running stack (research R7).
5. **User Story 4 specs are expected to pass when first run** (research R6): the page already has the behaviour. They are regression tests for the new error; a component is edited only if one of them fails.
6. `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `update-booking-result.dto.ts` hold no logic and get no spec of their own (plan.md).
7. T008 and T014 change existing specs so they keep passing with the new collaborators; they are not failing-first tasks.

---

## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)

**Purpose**: Confirm the starting point; the project, tooling and dependencies already exist.

- [ ] T001 Run `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` from the repository root (scripts in `package.json`) and confirm all three pass before any change; stop and report if one fails

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The one contract change and the two shared pieces both write paths use: the room lock with the overlap check, and the overlap rejection.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T002 Edit `libs/contract/src/lib/error-code.enum.ts`: add the member `BOOKING_OVERLAP = 'CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP'` on the line after `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`; change nothing else in `libs/contract`
- [ ] T003 [P] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.query.spec.ts` with an `EntityManager` whose `query` is a `jest.fn()`: `lockRoom(manager, roomId)` runs exactly one statement, `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0))`, with the parameters `['room:<roomId>']`, and two different room ids give two different lock names; `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, roomId, startsAt, endsAt, excludedBookingId)` runs exactly one statement whose text contains `"room_id" = $1`, `"starts_at" < $3`, `"ends_at" > $2` and `$4::uuid IS NULL OR "id" <> $4::uuid` and does not contain `confirmation_status`, with the parameters `[roomId, startsAt, endsAt, excludedBookingId]` (`null` passed through as `null`), and returns `true` for the row `[{ taken: true }]` and `false` for `[{ taken: false }]`
- [ ] T004 [P] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.error.spec.ts` (after T002): `raiseBookingOverlap()` throws an `RpcException` whose error is exactly `{ statusCode: 409, errorCode: ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP, message: 'The room is already booked for that time' }` (read the error the way the `errorOf` helper of `create-booking.service.spec.ts` does)
- [ ] T005 [P] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.query.ts` exporting `lockRoom(manager: EntityManager, roomId: string): Promise<void>` (kind: transaction-scoped advisory lock, waiting (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`); name: `room:<roomId>`, hashed with `hashtextextended(…, 0)`) and `isRoomSpanTaken(manager: EntityManager, roomId: string, startsAt: Date, endsAt: Date, excludedBookingId: string | null): Promise<boolean>` (`SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "bookings" WHERE "room_id" = $1 AND "starts_at" < $3 AND "ends_at" > $2 AND ($4::uuid IS NULL OR "id" <> $4::uuid)) AS "taken"`): a stored booking `b` is in the way when `b.room_id = R AND b.starts_at < end AND b.ends_at > start`, and, on update, `b.id` is not the booking being changed; both are plain functions, not providers (T003 passes)
- [ ] T006 [P] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.error.ts` exporting `raiseBookingOverlap(): never`, one statement: `ExceptionHelper.conflict(ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP, 'The room is already booked for that time')` (T004 passes; depends on T002)

**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run test` pass; user story work can begin.

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 - A room cannot be double-booked on create (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: `POST /api/bookings` for a span that overlaps a booking of the same room is answered 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; nothing is stored against the booking, the `Idempotency-Key` or the queue. Touching spans and other rooms are still accepted.

**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create a booking for a room, then send creates for the same room that overlap it, touch it and sit in another room, and reuse the key of a rejected create (quickstart scenarios 1, 2 and 3).

### Tests for User Story 1 (write first, must fail) ⚠️

- [ ] T007 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts` with the `DataSource`, query runner and `manager` mocked as in `idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts` and `./booking-overlap.query` mocked with `jest.mock`: (a) free span — `claim` calls `lockRoom(manager, booking.roomId)` then `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, booking.roomId, new Date(booking.startsAt), new Date(booking.endsAt), null)`, in this order by `invocationCallOrder`: `manager.findOneBy` (stored key) → `lockRoom` → `isRoomSpanTaken` → `manager.save`, and answers `CREATED`; (b) `isRoomSpanTaken` resolves `true` — the result is `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }`, `manager.save` and `manager.insert` are not called, the transaction is committed once, not rolled back, and the runner released once; (c) for each of `IN_PROGRESS` (first try-lock not obtained), `KEY_REUSED` (second try-lock not obtained), `REPLAYED` (stored row, same fingerprint) and `KEY_REUSED` (stored row, other fingerprint) neither `lockRoom` nor `isRoomSpanTaken` is called
- [ ] T008 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts`: add `jest.mock('./booking-overlap.query')` and, in `beforeEach`, make `isRoomSpanTaken` resolve `false` and `lockRoom` resolve; change no existing case and keep the file under 200 lines
- [ ] T009 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.spec.ts`: in `claim outcomes` add a failing case — a claim `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }` raises 409 with `errorCode` `ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and the message `The room is already booked for that time`, and `ConfirmationQueueProducer.enqueue` is not called; in `the same key after a rejected request` add a failing case — after an `OVERLAP` claim, the same key and body with the claim still `OVERLAP` raises the same 409 again (not a replay), and the same key with a claim that answers `CREATED` returns `{ booking, replayed: false }` and enqueues exactly one job

### Implementation for User Story 1

- [ ] T010 [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/claim-booking-result.dto.ts`: add `OVERLAP = 'OVERLAP'` to `ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum` after `IN_PROGRESS`
- [ ] T011 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.ts`: in `claimWithin`, after the stored-key branch and before `insertBookingWithKey`, call `lockRoom(manager, booking.roomId)`, then `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, booking.roomId, new Date(booking.startsAt), new Date(booking.endsAt), null)`, and return `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }` when it is `true`; the order inside the transaction is: try-lock key+fingerprint → try-lock key → read stored key → lock room (waits) → overlap check → insert booking + idempotency row (T007 passes, T008 stays green; depends on T005, T010)
- [ ] T012 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.ts`: in `toResult`, after the `IN_PROGRESS` branch, call `raiseBookingOverlap()` when the outcome is `ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP`; the enqueue stays limited to outcome `CREATED` and the order of the earlier checks (stored key, time pair, room) is not changed (T009 passes; depends on T006, T010)

**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run test` passes; quickstart scenarios 1, 2 and 3 pass against the running stack.

---

## Phase 4: User Story 2 - A room cannot be double-booked by moving a booking (Priority: P2)

**Goal**: `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` whose resulting span overlaps another booking of the same room is answered 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and leaves the booking unchanged; 404 and 400 are answered as before and win over overlap; a booking never conflicts with itself.

**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create two bookings of one room that do not overlap, then update one with times that overlap the other, touch the other and stay within its own span (quickstart scenario 4).

### Tests for User Story 2 (write first, must fail) ⚠️

- [ ] T013 [P] [US2] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.update.spec.ts` for `BookingRepository.update(id, changes)`, with the `BookingEntity` repository token mocked, the `DataSource` mocked as a query runner whose `manager` has `findOneBy` and `query` (pattern of `idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts`), and `./booking-overlap.query` mocked; the stored booking is 09:00–10:00 in room `R`: (a) first read finds no row → `{ outcome: NOT_FOUND, booking: null }`, `lockRoom` not called; (b) the read after the lock finds no row → `NOT_FOUND`; (c) `{ endsAt: 09:00 }` and `{ startsAt: 10:30 }` → `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` (resulting `ends_at` not later than resulting `starts_at`; the stored value is used for the time that was not sent), `isRoomSpanTaken` not called; (d) `isRoomSpanTaken` resolves `true` → `OVERLAP` with `booking: null` and no `UPDATE`; (e) `{ endsAt: 11:00 }` → `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, R, stored start, 11:00, id)` and one `UPDATE "bookings"` whose text still contains `"title" = COALESCE($2::varchar, "title")`, `"starts_at" = COALESCE($3::timestamptz, "starts_at")`, `"ends_at" = COALESCE($4::timestamptz, "ends_at")`, `"updated_at" = now()`, `COALESCE($4::timestamptz, "ends_at") > COALESCE($3::timestamptz, "starts_at")` and `RETURNING`, with the parameters `[id, null, null, new Date(11:00)]`, answering `{ outcome: UPDATED, booking: <returned row> }`; (f) a title-only change takes the lock and checks the stored span; (g) the `UPDATE` returns no row → `NOT_FOUND`; (h) order by `invocationCallOrder`: first read → `lockRoom(manager, R)` → second read → `isRoomSpanTaken` → `UPDATE`; (i) every outcome commits once and releases once; a statement that rejects rolls back, releases and rethrows
- [ ] T014 [P] [US2] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.spec.ts`: remove the `updateIfTimeRangeValid` describe (its SQL assertions now live in T013) and add `{ provide: DataSource, useValue: { createQueryRunner: jest.fn() } }` to the providers; change no other case
- [ ] T015 [P] [US2] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.service.spec.ts`: mock `BookingRepository.update` in place of `updateIfTimeRangeValid` and replace the three cases that follow the repository update with four failing ones — `UPDATED` returns the mapped DTO; `NOT_FOUND` raises 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` (`Booking not found`); `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` raises 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` (`endsAt must be later than startsAt`); `OVERLAP` raises 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` (`The room is already booked for that time`) — and in all four `findById` is not called; the no-field case (stored booking returned, `update` not called) and the unparsable-time case (400, `update` not called) stay as they are

### Implementation for User Story 2

- [ ] T016 [US2] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/update-booking-result.dto.ts` exporting `enum UpdateBookingOutcomeEnum { UPDATED, NOT_FOUND, INVALID_TIME_RANGE, OVERLAP }` (string values equal to the names) and `class UpdateBookingResultDto { outcome: UpdateBookingOutcomeEnum; booking: BookingEntity | null }`

## Phase 5: User Story 3 - Two people cannot take the same room at the same moment (Priority: P3)

**Independent Test**: Send two overlapping creates for the same room at the same moment, each with its own `Idempotency-Key`, 100 times; after every round count the answers and the stored bookings (quickstart scenario 5).

## Phase 7: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Purpose**: The completion gates and the end-to-end proof that nothing else changed.

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: no dependencies.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: after Setup; blocks every user story. T002 → T004 → T006; T003 → T005.
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: after Foundational.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: after Foundational; shares no file with User Story 1.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: T019 and T020 after User Story 1; T021 after User Stories 1 and 2.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: after T002 only (its mocks use `ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP`); shares no file with the backend stories.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: after every story.

### User Story Dependencies

```text
Setup → Foundational ─┬─▶ US1 (create) ──┬─▶ US3 (race proof: T019, T020)
                      │                  └─▶ ┐
                      ├─▶ US2 (update) ──────┴─▶ US3 (T021)
                      └─▶ US4 (page tests)
                                   all ─▶ Polish
```

- **US1 (P1)**: independent; the MVP.
- **US2 (P2)**: independent of US1 in code; delivered second because it closes the bypass of US1.
- **US3 (P3)**: depends on US1 (and on US2 for T021); it proves, it does not build.
- **US4 (P4)**: independent in code; meaningful by hand (T030) only once US1 and US2 run.

### Within Each User Story

- Spec tasks first; a "failing" spec MUST fail before its implementation task starts.
- DTO (T010, T016) before the repository and the service that use it.
- Repository and service of one story are in different files and can be done in parallel once the DTO exists.
- Story complete, with its checkpoint, before the next priority.

### Parallel Opportunities

- Phase 2: T003 and T004 together; then T005 and T006 together.
- US1: T007, T008 and T009 together; after T010, T011 and T012 together.
- US2: T013, T014 and T015 together; after T016, T017 and T018 together.
- US4: T022, T023 and T024 together.
- After Foundational, US1, US2 and US4 can be worked on at the same time: they share no file.
- Polish: T027 and T028 together.

---

## Parallel Example: User Story 1

```bash
# Specs of User Story 1 together:
Task: "Write the failing spec apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts"
Task: "Edit apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts to mock ./booking-overlap.query"
Task: "Add the OVERLAP cases to apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.spec.ts"

# After T010, the two implementations together:
Task: "Take the room lock and check the span in apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.ts"
Task: "Map OVERLAP to 409 in apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.ts"
```

## Parallel Example: User Story 2

```bash
# Specs of User Story 2 together:
Task: "Write the failing spec apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.update.spec.ts"
Task: "Edit apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.spec.ts (remove the old update describe, provide DataSource)"
Task: "Replace the update cases in apps/booking/src/booking/booking.service.spec.ts"

# After T016, the two implementations together:
Task: "Add the transactional update to apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.ts"
Task: "Map the update outcome in apps/booking/src/booking/booking.service.ts"
```

## Parallel Example: User Story 4

```bash
Task: "Write apps/web/src/views/bookings/booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx"
Task: "Add the overlap case to apps/web/src/views/bookings/booking-edit-dialog.spec.tsx"
Task: "Write apps/web/src/views/bookings/bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Phase 1: Setup (T001).
2. Phase 2: Foundational (T002–T006).
3. Phase 3: User Story 1 (T007–T012).
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: `pnpm run test`, then quickstart scenarios 1 to 3.

At this point a room can no longer be double-booked by a create, also under a race; it can still be double-booked by moving a booking until User Story 2 is done.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → the error code, the lock, the check and the rejection exist.
2. User Story 1 → create is safe (MVP).
3. User Story 2 → update is safe; the rule can no longer be bypassed.
4. User Story 3 → the race is proven against the running stack.
5. User Story 4 → the page behaviour is pinned by tests.
6. Polish → gates, scope check, full quickstart.

### Parallel Team Strategy

After Foundational, three people can take User Story 1, User Story 2 and User Story 4 at once; User Story 3 follows when 1 and 2 are merged.

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks touch different files and depend on no incomplete task.
- Requirement coverage: FR-001 to FR-004 → T003, T005; FR-005 to FR-008 → T007 to T012; FR-009 to FR-011 → T013 to T018; FR-012 to FR-014 → T007, T011, T013, T017, T019 to T021; FR-015, FR-016 → T002, T004, T006; FR-017 to FR-019 → T022 to T025; FR-020 to FR-025 → T026 to T030.
- A spec that fails for a reason other than the missing behaviour is fixed before the implementation starts.
- No commit task is listed: git is local and the owner decides when to commit.
- Stop at any checkpoint to validate the story on its own.

2. **Create** — the existing claim transaction in the `booking` service takes a per-room advisory
   lock, checks the span and returns a new outcome `OVERLAP` before anything is inserted, so a
   rejected create leaves no booking, no idempotency row and no job.
3. **Update** — the repository's update becomes one transaction under the same room lock that
   returns an outcome (updated, not found, invalid time pair, overlap); the service maps it to the
   answer.
4. **Bookings page** — the page already shows the API's message inside the form and keeps the
   input for any answered error; the change adds tests that pin this for the overlap rejection.

No table, migration, dependency, route or message pattern is added. Design decisions and their
reasons are in [research.md](./research.md).

**Primary Dependencies**: NestJS 11 (HTTP gateway, NATS microservices), TypeORM 0.3, class-validator / class-transformer, Next.js 15 (pages router) with React 18 and MUI 5, react-hook-form with yup — all already installed; no dependency is added

**Testing**: Jest 29 through Nx (`pnpm run test`); `@nestjs/testing` with the database mocked for the backend, Testing Library with the service layer mocked for the web page; races are proven against the running stack (quickstart)

**Project Type**: Web application in an Nx monorepo — HTTP gateway, NATS services, queue worker, Next.js frontend

**Performance Goals**: no throughput target; a writer waits only for another writer of the same room, for the length of one short transaction, well inside the gateway's 5-second NATS timeout

**Constraints**: the only contract change is the added error code (FR-015); `apps/room` and the `/rooms` page are not changed (FR-021); no data migration (FR-022); no new dependency; transactions only in repositories; every code file under 200 lines; `.env` files are never read

## Assumptions made in this plan

These fill gaps the specification leaves open; each takes the simplest option.

1. The rule is enforced by the `booking` service under a per-room lock, not by a database
   constraint. The service is the only writer of `bookings`.
2. No schema change is made, so there is no migration at all — stricter than FR-022, which forbids
   only migrating existing data.
3. The message is `The room is already booked for that time`, the same on create and update.
4. `BOOKING_OVERLAP` is placed after `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` in the enum, next to the other
   `CONFLICT.*` code.
5. Every update that changes something goes through the lock and the check, including a
   title-only update; an empty update still returns the stored booking without a transaction.
6. `updateIfTimeRangeValid` is replaced, not kept beside the new method; `BookingService` is its
   only caller.
7. A writer waits for the room lock without a timeout of its own; the wait is bounded by the other
   writer's short transaction.
8. Deletes take no lock.
9. The race (SC-003) is proven against the running stack in the quickstart; unit tests cover each
   outcome and the order of statements with the database mocked, as in `specs/001-room-bookings`.
10. No production code in `apps/web` changes, because the page already meets FR-017 to FR-019; if a
    new test shows otherwise, the component is fixed.
11. The gateway needs no new test: it forwards the rejection through the same path as every other
    error, which its existing specs cover.

91	### Edge Cases
92	
93	- **Overlap of a single instant**: spans are half-open, so 10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00 do not overlap; 10:00–11:00 and 10:59:59.999–12:00 do.
94	- **More than one existing booking is overlapped**: the answer is one 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; the conflicting bookings are not listed.
95	- **The overlapped booking's confirmation state**: irrelevant; a booking blocks its span whether it is `PENDING`, `SENT` or `FAILED`.
96	- **Bookings in the past**: they are still accepted and are subject to the same rule.
97	- **Create that is invalid and would also overlap**: the earlier checks win in their existing order — `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`, then `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`, then `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` — and overlap is checked last.
98	- **Update of a booking that does not exist, or with invalid times, that would also overlap**: answered 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` or 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` as today; overlap is checked last.
99	- **Update with an empty body**: still answered 200 with the booking unchanged.
100	- **Same key reused with a different body after an overlap rejection**: the rejected request stored nothing, so the new body is a first request; no 422.
101	- **Same key arrives again while the first request with it is still being processed**: answered as today (422 on a different body, otherwise 409 `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`), whether or not the first request ends in an overlap rejection.
102	- **Two identical creates with the same key at the same moment**: unchanged; exactly one booking, and the other request gets the replay or `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`, never `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` caused by its own twin.
103	- **A replay after the booking was deleted and its span taken by another booking**: the originally stored 201 is still replayed unchanged; a replay creates nothing, so no overlap check applies.
104	- **An update racing with a create or another update for the same room**: at most one of two changes that would overlap each other succeeds; the other is answered 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
105	- **A delete racing with a create for the same span**: the create is answered 201 or 409 depending on which is processed first; both outcomes are correct.
106	- **Other failures on the page (validation, unknown room, network error)**: shown as they are today; this change adds no new behaviour for them.

113	
114	- **FR-001**: Two bookings overlap when they are for the same room and each one starts before the other ends. Spans are half-open: a booking that starts exactly when another ends, or ends exactly when another starts, does not overlap it.
115	- **FR-002**: The system MUST never hold two overlapping bookings of the same room as a result of any create or update accepted after this change.
116	- **FR-003**: Bookings of different rooms MUST never conflict with each other, whatever their spans.
117	- **FR-004**: Only bookings that currently exist count. A deleted booking MUST NOT block anything, and a booking's confirmation state MUST NOT affect the rule.
118	
119	**Create**
120	
121	- **FR-005**: `POST /api/bookings` for a span that overlaps an existing booking of the same room MUST be answered with 409 and `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` where `errorCode` is `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
122	- **FR-006**: A create rejected for overlap MUST store no booking and MUST NOT enqueue a confirmation job.
123	- **FR-007**: A create rejected for overlap MUST NOT be stored against its `Idempotency-Key`: the key MUST remain usable, a later request with it MUST be treated as a first request, and the rejection MUST never be answered as a replay.
124	- **FR-008**: The overlap check MUST come after the existing create checks, so that an invalid key, an invalid body or an unknown room is answered exactly as before.

129	- **FR-010**: A booking MUST never conflict with itself. Changing only its title, shortening it within its own span, or moving it to a span that overlaps only its own previous span MUST succeed.

182	- **Relation to `specs/001-room-bookings`**: this change replaces that specification's "no overlap rule" assumption and its edge case "both are accepted", and lifts its ban on changing the shared contract for the one added error code. Everything else there still applies. That specification's files are not edited.
183	- **Rooms cannot be changed on update**: an update can change only `title`, `startsAt` and `endsAt`, so an update is only ever checked against the booking's own room.
184	- **Order of checks**: the description does not rank the overlap error against the existing errors. The simplest reading is used: the existing checks keep their order and overlap is checked last, on both create and update.
185	- **Update is checked on its resulting span**: every update is checked with the times the booking would have afterwards, against all other bookings of the room. A title-only update therefore always succeeds on data that respects the rule.
186	- **Races that involve an update**: the description names only two simultaneous creates. "That must stop" is read as covering updates as well, so the same guarantee is required for an update racing with a create or another update.
187	- **A rejected create and its key**: "not a stored idempotent response" is read as the existing rule for failed validation: nothing is stored against the key and the key can be used again with any body.
188	- **Replays are not re-checked**: a replay of a completed create returns the stored answer and creates nothing, so the overlap rule does not apply to it.
189	- **Message wording**: the exact text of the message is not prescribed; it only has to tell the person that the room is already booked for that time. The page shows whatever the API sends.
190	- **Conflicting bookings are not disclosed**: the rejection does not say which booking is in the way.
191	- **"Next to the form"**: the message appears inside or directly beside the form that was submitted (the create form, or the edit form of the row), not only in a page-level error area.
192	- **Page tests**: the page behaviour is covered by tests with the service layer mocked, in the same way as the existing page tests.
193	- **Existing data**: the database is reset before this change is used, so no stored bookings overlap when it starts and none need repair.
194	- **Past bookings and sign-in**: unchanged; bookings in the past are accepted and there is no authentication.
195	- **Dependencies**: the existing gateway, `booking`, `room` and `worker` services, their database, message bus and queue, and the shared contract are used as they are; no new dependency is added.
196	- **Technical terms in this specification**: routes, status codes, error codes, the header name, the contract location and the three commands come verbatim from the feature description's stated external behaviour and are kept so that the specification stays testable.

# Feature Specification: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Feature Branch**: none — no branch hook is installed; the work stays on `main` (feature directory `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap`)

**Created**: 2026-11-10

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Change: bookings for the same room may no longer overlap. Today two bookings can occupy the same room at the same time. That must stop." The description has a list of required behaviour (create and update rejected with 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, half-open time spans, no self-conflict, other rooms unaffected, simultaneous creates, everything else unchanged), one contract change (the new error code), one frontend rule (show the API's message next to the form and keep the input), a scope limit (the `room` service and the `/rooms` page are not changed; no data migration) and a definition of done. Every rule it states is carried into this specification.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - A room cannot be double-booked on create (Priority: P1)

A person who tries to book a room for a time span that is already taken, fully or partly, by another booking of that room is told so, and no booking is made. A span that only touches an existing booking, or the same span in another room, is still accepted.

**Why this priority**: This is the change. A room that two groups both hold for the same time is the failure the feature exists to stop, and create is where almost every booking comes from.

**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create a booking for a room, then send further creates for the same room that overlap it, touch it, and sit in another room, and compare each answer with the scenarios below.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a booking of room R from 10:00 to 11:00, **When** a create for room R from 10:30 to 11:30 is sent, **Then** the answer is 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and no booking is stored.
2. **Given** a booking of room R from 10:00 to 11:00, **When** a create for room R with exactly the same span, a span inside it (10:15 to 10:45) or a span that contains it (09:00 to 12:00) is sent, **Then** each is answered 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
3. **Given** a booking of room R from 10:00 to 11:00, **When** a create for room R from 11:00 to 12:00 is sent, **Then** the answer is 201: a booking that starts exactly when another ends does not overlap it.
4. **Given** a booking of room R from 10:00 to 11:00, **When** a create for room R from 09:00 to 10:00 is sent, **Then** the answer is 201: a booking that ends exactly when another starts does not overlap it.
5. **Given** a booking of room R from 10:00 to 11:00, **When** a create for a different room S from 10:00 to 11:00 is sent, **Then** the answer is 201.
6. **Given** a booking of room R that has since been deleted, **When** a create for room R with the same span is sent, **Then** the answer is 201: a deleted booking blocks nothing.
7. **Given** a create that was rejected for overlap, **When** the system is inspected, **Then** no booking exists for that request, no confirmation job was enqueued for it, and nothing is stored against its `Idempotency-Key`.
8. **Given** a create that was rejected for overlap, **When** the same `Idempotency-Key` is sent again with a body whose span is free, **Then** it is treated as a first request and the answer is 201.
9. **Given** a create that was rejected for overlap, **When** the same `Idempotency-Key` and the same body are sent again while the conflicting booking still exists, **Then** the answer is again 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and is not marked as replayed.
10. **Given** a create that succeeded, **When** the same `Idempotency-Key` and body are sent again, **Then** the stored answer is replayed unchanged, exactly as before this change.

---

### User Story 2 - A room cannot be double-booked by moving a booking (Priority: P2)

A person who changes the times of a booking so that it would run into another booking of the same room is told so, and the booking stays as it was. Changes that stay clear of other bookings, including changes inside the booking's own span, still succeed.

**Why this priority**: Without it, the rule of User Story 1 can be bypassed by creating a booking in a free span and then moving it.

**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create two bookings of one room that do not overlap, then update one of them with times that overlap the other, touch the other, and stay within its own span, and compare each answer with the scenarios below.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** bookings A (10:00 to 11:00) and B (11:00 to 12:00) of room R, **When** A's end is changed to 11:30, **Then** the answer is 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and A is unchanged.
2. **Given** bookings A (10:00 to 11:00) and B (12:00 to 13:00) of room R, **When** only B's start is changed to 10:30, **Then** the answer is 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and B is unchanged: the rule applies to the resulting stored pair of times, including when only one of them was sent.
3. **Given** bookings A (10:00 to 11:00) and B (12:00 to 13:00) of room R, **When** A's end is changed to 12:00, **Then** the answer is 200: A now ends exactly when B starts.
4. **Given** a booking A, **When** only its title is changed, **Then** the answer is 200.
5. **Given** a booking A (10:00 to 11:00), **When** its times are changed to 10:15 to 10:45, **Then** the answer is 200: a booking never conflicts with itself.
6. **Given** a booking A (10:00 to 11:00) with no neighbours in room R, **When** its times are changed to 10:30 to 11:30, **Then** the answer is 200: overlapping its own previous span is not a conflict.
7. **Given** booking A of room R and booking C of room S with the same span, **When** A's times are changed to any span that is free in room R, **Then** the answer is 200 regardless of C.

---

### User Story 3 - Two people cannot take the same room at the same moment (Priority: P3)

When two overlapping create requests for the same room arrive at the same moment, one person gets the room and the other is told it is taken. The room never ends up with both bookings.

**Why this priority**: The rule of User Story 1 is only trustworthy if it also holds when requests race; it builds on that story and matters under load rather than in everyday single use.

**Independent Test**: Send two overlapping creates for the same room at the same moment, each with its own `Idempotency-Key`, many times over; after every round count the answers and the stored bookings.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a free span in room R, **When** two overlapping creates for room R with different `Idempotency-Key` values arrive at the same moment, **Then** exactly one is answered 201 and the other is answered 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
2. **Given** the race of scenario 1 has finished, **When** the system is inspected, **Then** exactly one booking exists for that span, exactly one confirmation job was enqueued, and only the successful request's key holds a stored response.
3. **Given** two creates for different rooms with the same span arriving at the same moment, **When** both are processed, **Then** both are answered 201.
4. **Given** two creates for the same room whose spans only touch arriving at the same moment, **When** both are processed, **Then** both are answered 201.

---

### User Story 4 - See the conflict on the Bookings page without losing the input (Priority: P4)

A person who submits the create form or saves an edit on the `/bookings` page and is rejected for overlap sees the API's message next to the form they were filling in, with everything they typed still there, so they can pick another time and try again.

**Why this priority**: It is the human-facing surface of stories 1 and 2 and needs them to exist first.

**Independent Test**: With the service layer mocked to answer an overlap rejection, render the page, submit the create form and save an edit, and check the message and the kept values. Against a running system, do the same by hand at `/bookings`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the create form filled in, **When** it is submitted and the API rejects it for overlap, **Then** the API's `message` is shown next to the create form and the room, title, organizer email, start and end still hold what the person typed.
2. **Given** a row being edited, **When** the edit is saved and the API rejects it for overlap, **Then** the API's `message` is shown next to the edit form, the edit form stays open and its title, start and end still hold what the person typed.
3. **Given** an overlap message is shown next to a form, **When** the person changes the times to a free span and submits again, **Then** the request succeeds, the message disappears and the table shows the new or updated booking.
4. **Given** a create that was rejected for overlap, **When** the form is submitted again, **Then** that is a new submission with a new `Idempotency-Key`, as for any request the API answered.
5. **Given** an edit that was rejected for overlap, **When** the table is looked at, **Then** the row still shows the booking's stored values.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Overlap of a single instant**: spans are half-open, so 10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00 do not overlap; 10:00–11:00 and 10:59:59.999–12:00 do.
- **More than one existing booking is overlapped**: the answer is one 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; the conflicting bookings are not listed.
- **The overlapped booking's confirmation state**: irrelevant; a booking blocks its span whether it is `PENDING`, `SENT` or `FAILED`.
- **Bookings in the past**: they are still accepted and are subject to the same rule.
- **Create that is invalid and would also overlap**: the earlier checks win in their existing order — `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`, then `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`, then `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` — and overlap is checked last.
- **Update of a booking that does not exist, or with invalid times, that would also overlap**: answered 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` or 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` as today; overlap is checked last.
- **Update with an empty body**: still answered 200 with the booking unchanged.
- **Same key reused with a different body after an overlap rejection**: the rejected request stored nothing, so the new body is a first request; no 422.
- **Same key arrives again while the first request with it is still being processed**: answered as today (422 on a different body, otherwise 409 `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`), whether or not the first request ends in an overlap rejection.
- **Two identical creates with the same key at the same moment**: unchanged; exactly one booking, and the other request gets the replay or `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`, never `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` caused by its own twin.
- **A replay after the booking was deleted and its span taken by another booking**: the originally stored 201 is still replayed unchanged; a replay creates nothing, so no overlap check applies.
- **An update racing with a create or another update for the same room**: at most one of two changes that would overlap each other succeeds; the other is answered 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
- **A delete racing with a create for the same span**: the create is answered 201 or 409 depending on which is processed first; both outcomes are correct.
- **Other failures on the page (validation, unknown room, network error)**: shown as they are today; this change adds no new behaviour for them.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

**Overlap rule**

- **FR-001**: Two bookings overlap when they are for the same room and each one starts before the other ends. Spans are half-open: a booking that starts exactly when another ends, or ends exactly when another starts, does not overlap it.
- **FR-002**: The system MUST never hold two overlapping bookings of the same room as a result of any create or update accepted after this change.
- **FR-003**: Bookings of different rooms MUST never conflict with each other, whatever their spans.
- **FR-004**: Only bookings that currently exist count. A deleted booking MUST NOT block anything, and a booking's confirmation state MUST NOT affect the rule.

**Create**

- **FR-005**: `POST /api/bookings` for a span that overlaps an existing booking of the same room MUST be answered with 409 and `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` where `errorCode` is `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
- **FR-006**: A create rejected for overlap MUST store no booking and MUST NOT enqueue a confirmation job.
- **FR-007**: A create rejected for overlap MUST NOT be stored against its `Idempotency-Key`: the key MUST remain usable, a later request with it MUST be treated as a first request, and the rejection MUST never be answered as a replay.
- **FR-008**: The overlap check MUST come after the existing create checks, so that an invalid key, an invalid body or an unknown room is answered exactly as before.

**Update**

- **FR-009**: `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` MUST be answered with 409 and `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` when the resulting stored span of the booking would overlap another booking of the same room, including when only one of the two times was sent. The booking MUST then be unchanged.
- **FR-010**: A booking MUST never conflict with itself. Changing only its title, shortening it within its own span, or moving it to a span that overlaps only its own previous span MUST succeed.
- **FR-011**: The overlap check MUST come after the existing update checks, so that an unknown booking or an invalid pair of times is answered exactly as before.

**Simultaneous requests**

- **FR-012**: When two overlapping creates for the same room arrive at the same moment, exactly one MUST be answered 201 and the other MUST be answered 409 with `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`. The loser MUST leave no booking, no confirmation job and no stored idempotent response.
- **FR-013**: The guarantee of FR-002 MUST also hold when an update races with a create or with another update for the same room.
- **FR-014**: Simultaneous requests for different rooms, or for spans of the same room that do not overlap, MUST NOT be rejected because of each other.

**Contract**

- **FR-015**: The error code `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` MUST be added to `ErrorCodeEnum` in the shared contract (`libs/contract`). This MUST be the only change to the contract.
- **FR-016**: The overlap rejection MUST carry a human-readable `message` that says the room is already booked for that time.

**Bookings page (`apps/web`)**

- **FR-017**: When a create on the `/bookings` page is rejected for overlap, the page MUST show the API's `message` next to the create form and MUST keep every value the person typed.
- **FR-018**: When an edit on the `/bookings` page is rejected for overlap, the page MUST show the API's `message` next to the edit form, keep the edit form open and keep every value the person typed.
- **FR-019**: The message MUST disappear once the form is submitted again successfully.

**Unchanged behaviour and scope**

- **FR-020**: Everything else about bookings MUST stay as specified in `specs/001-room-bookings`: listing, reading, deleting, validation, the idempotent create (replay, 422 on a reused key, 409 while in progress, keys that never expire) and the confirmation job.
- **FR-021**: The `room` service and the `/rooms` page MUST NOT be changed.
- **FR-022**: No migration or clean-up of existing data MUST be part of this change.

**Completion**

- **FR-023**: The behaviour above MUST hold end to end through the gateway.
- **FR-024**: New and changed services MUST have unit tests.
- **FR-025**: `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` MUST pass.

### Key Entities

- **Booking**: one reservation of one room for a half-open time span, from its start up to but not including its end. Unchanged in shape; it gains the rule that no other booking of the same room may share any part of its span.
- **Room**: the scope of the overlap rule. Bookings are compared only with bookings of the same room. Read-only for this change.
- **Overlap rejection**: the error answer given when a create or update would break the rule: status 409, the new error code `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and a message for the person.
- **Idempotency record**: unchanged. It is written only for creates that succeed, so an overlap rejection never has one.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: After any sequence of creates and updates, the number of pairs of overlapping bookings in the same room is 0.
- **SC-002**: 100% of creates and updates that would overlap another booking of the same room are answered with the overlap rejection, and 100% of those that only touch another booking, stay within their own span, or concern another room are accepted.
- **SC-003**: In 100 rounds of two overlapping creates for the same room sent at the same moment, every round ends with exactly 1 success, exactly 1 overlap rejection, exactly 1 stored booking and exactly 1 confirmation job.
- **SC-004**: After any rejected create, 0 bookings, 0 confirmation jobs and 0 stored idempotent responses exist for that request.
- **SC-005**: On the Bookings page, a person whose create or edit was rejected for overlap can correct the time and submit again without retyping any other field, in 100% of cases.
- **SC-006**: Every behaviour of bookings that this specification does not change gives the same answers as before the change.
- **SC-007**: The repository's build, lint and test commands all pass; the `room` service and the `/rooms` page show no changes; the shared contract shows exactly one change, the added error code.

## Assumptions

- **Relation to `specs/001-room-bookings`**: this change replaces that specification's "no overlap rule" assumption and its edge case "both are accepted", and lifts its ban on changing the shared contract for the one added error code. Everything else there still applies. That specification's files are not edited.
- **Rooms cannot be changed on update**: an update can change only `title`, `startsAt` and `endsAt`, so an update is only ever checked against the booking's own room.
- **Order of checks**: the description does not rank the overlap error against the existing errors. The simplest reading is used: the existing checks keep their order and overlap is checked last, on both create and update.
- **Update is checked on its resulting span**: every update is checked with the times the booking would have afterwards, against all other bookings of the room. A title-only update therefore always succeeds on data that respects the rule.
- **Races that involve an update**: the description names only two simultaneous creates. "That must stop" is read as covering updates as well, so the same guarantee is required for an update racing with a create or another update.
- **A rejected create and its key**: "not a stored idempotent response" is read as the existing rule for failed validation: nothing is stored against the key and the key can be used again with any body.
- **Replays are not re-checked**: a replay of a completed create returns the stored answer and creates nothing, so the overlap rule does not apply to it.
- **Message wording**: the exact text of the message is not prescribed; it only has to tell the person that the room is already booked for that time. The page shows whatever the API sends.
- **Conflicting bookings are not disclosed**: the rejection does not say which booking is in the way.
- **"Next to the form"**: the message appears inside or directly beside the form that was submitted (the create form, or the edit form of the row), not only in a page-level error area.
- **Page tests**: the page behaviour is covered by tests with the service layer mocked, in the same way as the existing page tests.
- **Existing data**: the database is reset before this change is used, so no stored bookings overlap when it starts and none need repair.
- **Past bookings and sign-in**: unchanged; bookings in the past are accepted and there is no authentication.
- **Dependencies**: the existing gateway, `booking`, `room` and `worker` services, their database, message bus and queue, and the shared contract are used as they are; no new dependency is added.
- **Technical terms in this specification**: routes, status codes, error codes, the header name, the contract location and the three commands come verbatim from the feature description's stated external behaviour and are kept so that the specification stays testable.

2

4

6	changed (FR-022). Everything in `specs/001-room-bookings/data-model.md` still applies; this document
7	lists only what is new.
8	
9	## Booking — table `bookings` (shape unchanged)
10	
11	### New rule: no overlap within a room
12	
13	Two bookings overlap when all of these hold (FR-001):
14	
15	- same `room_id`;
16	- `starts_at` of each is earlier than `ends_at` of the other;
17	- they are different rows.
18	
19	Spans are half-open, `[starts_at, ends_at)`: a booking that starts when another ends does not
20	overlap it. Only rows that exist count; `confirmation_status` plays no part (FR-004).
21	
22	For a candidate span `[start, end)` in room `R`, a stored booking `b` is in the way when
23	`b.room_id = R AND b.starts_at < end AND b.ends_at > start`, and, on update, `b.id` is not the
24	booking being changed. The existing index `IDX_bookings_room_id_starts_at` serves this lookup.
25	
26	### Added validation rules
27	
28	| Rule | Enforced by | Answer |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| A new booking's span is free in its room (FR-005) | claim transaction in `IdempotentBookingRepository`, under the room lock; the service chooses the answer | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
31	| An updated booking's resulting span is free in its room, itself excluded (FR-009, FR-010) | update transaction in `BookingRepository`, under the room lock; the service chooses the answer | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
32	
33	Both come after every existing rule in the 001 table (FR-008, FR-011).
34	
35	### Room lock
36	
37	| Property | Value |
38	|---|---|
39	| Kind | transaction-scoped advisory lock, waiting (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`) |
40	| Name | `room:<roomId>`, hashed with `hashtextextended(…, 0)` |
41	| Taken by | the create claim transaction and the update transaction, before the overlap check |
42	| Not taken by | list, read, delete, recording a confirmation outcome, a replay |
43	| Released | at commit or rollback |
44	
45	Nothing is stored for the lock.
46	
47	## Claim outcomes (create) — one added
48	
49	Internal to the `booking` service; not a contract item.
50	
51	| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| `CREATED`, `REPLAYED`, `KEY_REUSED`, `IN_PROGRESS` | as in 001 | as in 001 |
54	| `OVERLAP` *(new)* | the key is free and unclaimed, and the span is taken in the room | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; no booking, no idempotency row, no job |
55	
56	Order inside the claim transaction:
57	
58	```text
59	try-lock key+fingerprint ── not obtained ──▶ IN_PROGRESS
60	try-lock key ────────────── not obtained ──▶ KEY_REUSED
61	read stored key ─────────── found ─────────▶ REPLAYED / KEY_REUSED
62	lock room (waits)
63	overlap check ───────────── taken ─────────▶ OVERLAP        (nothing written)
64	insert booking + idempotency row ──────────▶ CREATED
65	```
66	
67	## Update outcomes — new
68	
69	Internal to the `booking` service. Class `UpdateBookingResultDto` with `UpdateBookingOutcomeEnum`
70	and the stored booking (or `null`).
71	
72	| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| `NOT_FOUND` | no booking with that id, before or after the wait for the lock | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
75	| `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` | resulting `ends_at` not later than resulting `starts_at` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
76	| `OVERLAP` | the resulting span is taken by another booking of the room | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; booking unchanged |
77	| `UPDATED` | none of the above | 200 with the stored booking |
78	
79	The resulting span uses the stored value for a time that was not sent. An update with no fields is
80	answered by the service before any transaction, as today.
81	
82	## Idempotency record — table `idempotency_keys` (unchanged)
83	
84	A row is still written only together with a booking. An overlap rejection writes none, so its key
85	stays usable with any body (FR-007).
86	
87	## Room — table `rooms` (read-only, unchanged)
88	
89	The scope of the rule. Not read, locked or written by this change; the room lock is a name derived
90	from the room's id, not a lock on its row.
91	
92	## Error code — `ErrorCodeEnum` (the one contract change)
93	
94	| Member | Value | Status |
95	|---|---|---|
96	| `BOOKING_OVERLAP` | `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` | 409 |
97	
98	## Migrations
99	
100	None.

# Data Model: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Feature**: `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap` | **Date**: 2026-11-10

This change adds a rule, not data. No table, column, constraint, index or migration is added or
changed (FR-022). Everything in `specs/001-room-bookings/data-model.md` still applies; this document
lists only what is new.

## Booking — table `bookings` (shape unchanged)

### New rule: no overlap within a room

Two bookings overlap when all of these hold (FR-001):

- same `room_id`;
- `starts_at` of each is earlier than `ends_at` of the other;
- they are different rows.

Spans are half-open, `[starts_at, ends_at)`: a booking that starts when another ends does not
overlap it. Only rows that exist count; `confirmation_status` plays no part (FR-004).

For a candidate span `[start, end)` in room `R`, a stored booking `b` is in the way when
`b.room_id = R AND b.starts_at < end AND b.ends_at > start`, and, on update, `b.id` is not the
booking being changed. The existing index `IDX_bookings_room_id_starts_at` serves this lookup.

### Added validation rules

| Rule | Enforced by | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| A new booking's span is free in its room (FR-005) | claim transaction in `IdempotentBookingRepository`, under the room lock; the service chooses the answer | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
| An updated booking's resulting span is free in its room, itself excluded (FR-009, FR-010) | update transaction in `BookingRepository`, under the room lock; the service chooses the answer | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |

Both come after every existing rule in the 001 table (FR-008, FR-011).

### Room lock

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | transaction-scoped advisory lock, waiting (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`) |
| Name | `room:<roomId>`, hashed with `hashtextextended(…, 0)` |
| Taken by | the create claim transaction and the update transaction, before the overlap check |
| Not taken by | list, read, delete, recording a confirmation outcome, a replay |
| Released | at commit or rollback |

Nothing is stored for the lock.

## Claim outcomes (create) — one added

Internal to the `booking` service; not a contract item.

| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `CREATED`, `REPLAYED`, `KEY_REUSED`, `IN_PROGRESS` | as in 001 | as in 001 |
| `OVERLAP` *(new)* | the key is free and unclaimed, and the span is taken in the room | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; no booking, no idempotency row, no job |

Order inside the claim transaction:

```text
try-lock key+fingerprint ── not obtained ──▶ IN_PROGRESS
try-lock key ────────────── not obtained ──▶ KEY_REUSED
read stored key ─────────── found ─────────▶ REPLAYED / KEY_REUSED
lock room (waits)
overlap check ───────────── taken ─────────▶ OVERLAP        (nothing written)
insert booking + idempotency row ──────────▶ CREATED
```

## Update outcomes — new

Internal to the `booking` service. Class `UpdateBookingResultDto` with `UpdateBookingOutcomeEnum`
and the stored booking (or `null`).

| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `NOT_FOUND` | no booking with that id, before or after the wait for the lock | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
| `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` | resulting `ends_at` not later than resulting `starts_at` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
| `OVERLAP` | the resulting span is taken by another booking of the room | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; booking unchanged |
| `UPDATED` | none of the above | 200 with the stored booking |

The resulting span uses the stored value for a time that was not sent. An update with no fields is
answered by the service before any transaction, as today.

## Idempotency record — table `idempotency_keys` (unchanged)

A row is still written only together with a booking. An overlap rejection writes none, so its key
stays usable with any body (FR-007).

## Room — table `rooms` (read-only, unchanged)

The scope of the rule. Not read, locked or written by this change; the room lock is a name derived
from the room's id, not a lock on its row.

## Error code — `ErrorCodeEnum` (the one contract change)

| Member | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `BOOKING_OVERLAP` | `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` | 409 |

## Migrations

None.

72	| room R, 09:00–10:00 | 201 (touching at the start) |
73	| room S, 10:00–11:00 | 201 (another room) |

105	S: `C` 10:00–11:00.
