108	|---|---|
109	| `B` with `{"startsAt":"…T10:30:00.000Z"}` | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; `GET` shows `B` unchanged |
110	| `A` with `{"endsAt":"…T12:30:00.000Z"}` | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; `A` unchanged |
111	| `A` with `{"endsAt":"…T12:00:00.000Z"}` | 200 (now ends when `B` starts) |
112	| `A` with `{"title":"Renamed"}` | 200 |
113	| `A` with `{"startsAt":"…T10:15:00.000Z","endsAt":"…T10:45:00.000Z"}` | 200 (inside its own span) |
114	| `A` with `{"startsAt":"…T10:30:00.000Z","endsAt":"…T11:30:00.000Z"}` | 200 (overlaps only its own previous span) |
115	| `A` with `{}` | 200, unchanged |
116	| `C` with `{"startsAt":"…T12:00:00.000Z","endsAt":"…T13:00:00.000Z"}` | 200 (room S; `B` is in room R) |
117	| `B` with `{"endsAt":"…T11:00:00.000Z"}` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` (invalid pair wins) |
118	| a random UUID with `{"startsAt":"…T10:30:00.000Z"}` | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |
119	
120	### 5. Two creates at the same moment (User Story 3, SC-003)
121	
122	One hundred rounds, each on its own day so rounds do not affect each other:
123	
124	```bash
125	for i in $(seq 1 100); do
126	  DAY=$(date -u -j -v+"${i}"d -f '%Y-%m-%d' 2031-06-01 '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || date -u -d "2031-06-01 +${i} day" '+%Y-%m-%d')
127	  ( book $ROOM_R ${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z ${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z | tail -1 & \
128	    book $ROOM_R ${DAY}T10:30:00.000Z ${DAY}T11:30:00.000Z | tail -1 & wait ) | sort | tr '\n' ' '; echo
129	done | sort | uniq -c
130	```
131	
132	Expected: one line, `100 201 409`.

135	
136	| Check | Expected |
137	|---|---|
138	| `curl -s "$API/bookings?roomId=$ROOM_R&limit=100" \| jq '.total'` (after a fresh reset) | 100 — one booking per round |
139	| the same bookings read 10 seconds later | every one `SENT` with 1 attempt: one confirmation job per stored booking |
140	| `tmp/logs/worker.log` | no job for a booking that does not exist |
141	
142	A rejected request has no booking id, so no job id can exist for it; with BullMQ's default key
143	prefix, `docker compose exec redis redis-cli ZCARD bull:booking-confirmation:completed` equals the

147	
148	| Two simultaneous creates | Expected |
149	|---|---|
150	| room R and room S, same span | `201 201` |
151	| room R, 10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00 | `201 201` |
152	| the same key and body twice | one booking; answers are 201 and either a replayed 201 or 409 `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` — never `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |

155

162	
163	Open `http://localhost:${WEB_PORT}/bookings` with one booking of room R, 10:00–11:00 local time.
164	
165	| Step | Expected |
166	|---|---|
167	| Fill the create form for room R, 10:30–11:30, submit | the API's message appears inside the form; all five fields keep their values; the table is unchanged |

# Quickstart: Validating the Overlap Rule

**Feature**: `specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap` | **Date**: 2026-11-10

A run guide that proves the change end to end. Answers and codes are in
[contracts/gateway-http-api.md](./contracts/gateway-http-api.md); page behaviour is in
[contracts/bookings-page.md](./contracts/bookings-page.md); the rule and its outcomes are in
[data-model.md](./data-model.md).

## Prerequisites

- Node 22 or newer, pnpm, Docker (see `docs/local-setup.md`).
- `curl`, `jq` and `uuidgen` for the HTTP scenarios.

## Automated gates

```bash
pnpm run build
pnpm run lint
pnpm run test
```

All three must pass (FR-025).

Scope check (FR-015, FR-021, FR-022, SC-007):

```bash
git status --porcelain -- apps/room apps/web/src/views/rooms apps/web/src/pages/rooms apps/web/src/services/room.service.ts libs/backend-common/src/lib/database
git diff --stat -- libs/contract
```

The first must print nothing. The second must show one file, `error-code.enum.ts`, with one added
line.

## Start the stack

```bash
pnpm run stack:reset    # fresh data: no stored bookings overlap when the change is first used
```

The shell needs the gateway and web ports, by name `GATEWAY_PORT` and `WEB_PORT`:

```bash
API="http://localhost:${GATEWAY_PORT}/api"
ROOM_R=$(curl -s "$API/rooms?limit=2" | jq -r '.items[0].id')
ROOM_S=$(curl -s "$API/rooms?limit=2" | jq -r '.items[1].id')

book() {  # book <roomId> <start> <end> [key] → prints the status and the body
  jq -n --arg r "$1" --arg s "$2" --arg e "$3" \
    '{roomId:$r,title:"Overlap check",organizerEmail:"qa.user+overlap@example.com",startsAt:$s,endsAt:$e}' |
  curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST "$API/bookings" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Idempotency-Key: ${4:-$(uuidgen)}" -d @-
}
```

## Scenarios

All times are on 2031-03-03, UTC. `D=2031-03-03T`.

### 1. Create (User Story 1)

Start with `book $ROOM_R ${D}10:00:00.000Z ${D}11:00:00.000Z` → 201. Keep its `id` as `A`.

| Request | Expected |
|---|---|
| room R, 10:30–11:30 | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, a `message` saying the room is already booked |
| room R, 10:00–11:00 | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
| room R, 10:15–10:45 | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
| room R, 09:00–12:00 | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
| room R, 10:59:59.999–12:00 | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |
| room R, 11:00–12:00 | 201 (touching at the end) |
| room R, 09:00–10:00 | 201 (touching at the start) |
| room S, 10:00–11:00 | 201 (another room) |

`GET $API/bookings?roomId=$ROOM_R` then shows three bookings (09–10, 10–11, 11–12), none overlapping.

Deleted bookings block nothing: `DELETE $API/bookings/$A`, then room R, 10:00–11:00 → 201.

### 2. Order of checks on create (FR-008)

Each would also overlap the 10:00–11:00 booking of room R:

| Request | Expected |
|---|---|
| no `Idempotency-Key` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` |
| `title` removed | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
| `endsAt` equal to `startsAt` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
| `roomId` a random UUID | 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` |

### 3. A rejected create and its key (User Story 1, scenarios 7–10)

```bash
KEY=$(uuidgen)
book $ROOM_R ${D}10:30:00.000Z ${D}11:30:00.000Z $KEY   # 409 CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP
book $ROOM_R ${D}10:30:00.000Z ${D}11:30:00.000Z $KEY   # 409 again; add -i to see no Idempotency-Replayed header
book $ROOM_R ${D}14:00:00.000Z ${D}15:00:00.000Z $KEY   # 201: the key was never stored, so no 422
book $ROOM_R ${D}14:00:00.000Z ${D}15:00:00.000Z $KEY   # 201 replayed, header Idempotency-Replayed: true
```

After the first two, the list shows no booking for 10:30–11:30.

### 4. Update (User Story 2)

On a fresh `pnpm run stack:reset`, create in room R: `A` 10:00–11:00 and `B` 12:00–13:00; in room
S: `C` 10:00–11:00.

| `PATCH` | Expected |
|---|---|
| `B` with `{"startsAt":"…T10:30:00.000Z"}` | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; `GET` shows `B` unchanged |
| `A` with `{"endsAt":"…T12:30:00.000Z"}` | 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; `A` unchanged |
| `A` with `{"endsAt":"…T12:00:00.000Z"}` | 200 (now ends when `B` starts) |
| `A` with `{"title":"Renamed"}` | 200 |
| `A` with `{"startsAt":"…T10:15:00.000Z","endsAt":"…T10:45:00.000Z"}` | 200 (inside its own span) |
| `A` with `{"startsAt":"…T10:30:00.000Z","endsAt":"…T11:30:00.000Z"}` | 200 (overlaps only its own previous span) |
| `A` with `{}` | 200, unchanged |
| `C` with `{"startsAt":"…T12:00:00.000Z","endsAt":"…T13:00:00.000Z"}` | 200 (room S; `B` is in room R) |
| `B` with `{"endsAt":"…T11:00:00.000Z"}` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` (invalid pair wins) |
| a random UUID with `{"startsAt":"…T10:30:00.000Z"}` | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |

### 5. Two creates at the same moment (User Story 3, SC-003)

One hundred rounds, each on its own day so rounds do not affect each other:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  DAY=$(date -u -j -v+"${i}"d -f '%Y-%m-%d' 2031-06-01 '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || date -u -d "2031-06-01 +${i} day" '+%Y-%m-%d')
  ( book $ROOM_R ${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z ${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z | tail -1 & \
    book $ROOM_R ${DAY}T10:30:00.000Z ${DAY}T11:30:00.000Z | tail -1 & wait ) | sort | tr '\n' ' '; echo
done | sort | uniq -c
```

Expected: one line, `100 201 409`.

Then:

| Check | Expected |
|---|---|
| `curl -s "$API/bookings?roomId=$ROOM_R&limit=100" \| jq '.total'` (after a fresh reset) | 100 — one booking per round |
| the same bookings read 10 seconds later | every one `SENT` with 1 attempt: one confirmation job per stored booking |
| `tmp/logs/worker.log` | no job for a booking that does not exist |

A rejected request has no booking id, so no job id can exist for it; with BullMQ's default key
prefix, `docker compose exec redis redis-cli ZCARD bull:booking-confirmation:completed` equals the
number of bookings created since the reset.

Variations, a few rounds each:

| Two simultaneous creates | Expected |
|---|---|
| room R and room S, same span | `201 201` |
| room R, 10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00 | `201 201` |
| the same key and body twice | one booking; answers are 201 and either a replayed 201 or 409 `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` — never `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` |

### 6. An update racing with a create (FR-013)

With `A` 10:00–11:00 in room R and 11:00–12:00 free, send at the same moment a `PATCH` of `A` with
`{"endsAt":"…T11:30:00.000Z"}` and a create for room R 11:00–12:00; repeat about 20 times, restoring
the starting state between rounds. Expected every round: exactly one of the two succeeds, the other
is 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, and the room's bookings never overlap.

### 7. Bookings page (User Story 4)

Open `http://localhost:${WEB_PORT}/bookings` with one booking of room R, 10:00–11:00 local time.

| Step | Expected |
|---|---|
| Fill the create form for room R, 10:30–11:30, submit | the API's message appears inside the form; all five fields keep their values; the table is unchanged |
| Change the times to a free span, submit | the message disappears, the form is cleared, the new booking is in the table; the network panel shows a different `Idempotency-Key` on the two requests |
| Create a second booking of room R, 12:00–13:00; edit it to start at 10:30, save | the message appears inside the edit dialog; the dialog stays open with the typed values; the row behind it shows the stored values |
| Change the start back to a free time, save | the dialog closes and the row shows the new values |
| Submit a create with the end before the start | the field error, as before; no request |

### 8. Nothing else changed (FR-020, SC-006)

Run scenarios 1 to 10 of `specs/001-room-bookings/quickstart.md` on a fresh reset, using a different
time span for each booking it creates in the same room. Every expected outcome there still holds.

## Clean up

```bash
pnpm run stack:down
```

The bookings created above are synthetic and live only in the local database; `pnpm run stack:reset`
removes them.

21	# roombook Constitution
22	
23	These rules apply to every change in this repository.
24	
25	## Core Principles
26	
27	### I. Contract as Source of Truth
28	
29	- `libs/contract` (`@roombook/contract`) is the source of truth for routes, message patterns,
30	  queue names, DTO classes, error codes and job payloads.
31	- Code MUST use what `@roombook/contract` exports. A route, pattern, field or error code
32	  MUST NOT be invented outside it.
33	- Errors MUST cross service boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`, with
34	  `errorCode` taken from `ErrorCodeEnum`.
35	
36	Rationale: the gateway, the NATS services, the worker and the frontend stay compatible only
37	when they all read the same definitions.
38	
39	### II. Layered Architecture
40	
41	- Controllers MUST be thin: at most five statements, all delegating to a service. Controllers
42	  MUST NOT contain logic.
43	- Every POST, PUT and PATCH handler MUST take a DTO class with class-validator decorators as
44	  its body.
45	- Services hold business rules and MUST delegate data access to repositories.
46	- Database transactions MUST live in repositories only, never in services.
47	- The gateway MUST NOT hold database access or business rules; it validates input and forwards
48	  over NATS.
49	- Every controller, service and provider MUST be registered in exactly one module.
50	- Source files MUST NOT contain literal ports, hosts, URLs or secrets; configuration comes from
51	  environment variables read through the config module.
52	- Every deployable service MUST have a health endpoint: a health message pattern on each NATS
53	  service, exposed by the gateway as `GET /api/health/<service>`.
54	
55	Rationale: each layer has one responsibility, so a rule has one place to live and one place
56	to be tested.
57	
58	### III. Strict TypeScript
59	
60	- `interface` MUST NOT be used; use `class` for DTOs and `type` for everything else.
61	- `any` MUST NOT be used.
62	- An inline object type MUST NOT be used as a function parameter; define a named DTO class.
63	- Every repository method MUST have an explicit return type.
64	- Imports MUST be named imports; `import * as` MUST NOT be used.
65	
66	Rationale: explicit, named types keep the contract visible at every boundary and stop
67	untyped data from leaking between layers.
68	
69	### IV. Small, Self-Describing Files
70	
71	- File names MUST be kebab-case and describe their purpose.
72	- Every code file MUST stay under 200 lines; split by concern.
73	- Comments MUST NOT restate what the code does. A comment is allowed only for a non-obvious
74	  constraint, in one short line.
75	
76	Rationale: a file whose name and size reveal its purpose can be found and understood without
77	opening its neighbours.
78	
79	### V. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
80	
81	- Every new or modified service MUST have at least one unit test in a `*.spec.ts` file next
82	  to it.
83	- The failing test MUST be written before the implementation.
84	
85	Rationale: a test written first proves the behaviour was missing and that the change added it.
86	
87	## Safety Constraints
88	
89	- `.env` and `.env.*` files MUST NOT be read; refer to configuration by variable name.
90	- Git is local only: no remote, no push, no pull request.
91	- Dependencies MUST NOT be added.
92	
93	## Quality Gates
94	
95	A change is finished only when all three commands pass:
96	
97	- `pnpm run build`
98	- `pnpm run lint`
99	- `pnpm run test`
100	
101	## Governance
102	
103	- This constitution supersedes any other practice in this repository. Where another document
104	  conflicts with it, the constitution wins.
105	- Amendments are made by editing this file through `/speckit-constitution`, with the change
106	  recorded in a local commit.
107	- Versions follow semantic versioning: MAJOR for removing or redefining a principle, MINOR for
108	  adding a principle or section or materially expanding guidance, PATCH for clarifications and
109	  wording.
110	- Every specification, plan, task list and implementation MUST be checked against these
111	  principles. A violation MUST be fixed, or justified in writing in the plan, before the
112	  change is considered finished.
113	
114	**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-11-10 | **Last Amended**: 2026-11-10
115

  - V. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- Added sections: Safety Constraints; Quality Gates; Governance
- Removed sections: none
- Assumptions:
  - The "Tests" rules are split: the two test-writing rules form Principle V, the
    build/lint/test completion rule forms the Quality Gates section.
  - Governance rules (amendment, versioning, compliance review) were not supplied and are
    the simplest set that satisfies the template.
  - Ratification date is the date of first adoption, 2026-11-10.
- Follow-up TODOs: none

# roombook Constitution

These rules apply to every change in this repository.

## Core Principles

### I. Contract as Source of Truth

- `libs/contract` (`@roombook/contract`) is the source of truth for routes, message patterns,
  queue names, DTO classes, error codes and job payloads.
- Code MUST use what `@roombook/contract` exports. A route, pattern, field or error code
  MUST NOT be invented outside it.
- Errors MUST cross service boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`, with
  `errorCode` taken from `ErrorCodeEnum`.

Rationale: the gateway, the NATS services, the worker and the frontend stay compatible only
when they all read the same definitions.

### II. Layered Architecture

- Controllers MUST be thin: at most five statements, all delegating to a service. Controllers
  MUST NOT contain logic.
- Every POST, PUT and PATCH handler MUST take a DTO class with class-validator decorators as
  its body.
- Services hold business rules and MUST delegate data access to repositories.
- Database transactions MUST live in repositories only, never in services.
- The gateway MUST NOT hold database access or business rules; it validates input and forwards
  over NATS.
- Every controller, service and provider MUST be registered in exactly one module.
- Source files MUST NOT contain literal ports, hosts, URLs or secrets; configuration comes from
  environment variables read through the config module.
- Every deployable service MUST have a health endpoint: a health message pattern on each NATS
  service, exposed by the gateway as `GET /api/health/<service>`.

Rationale: each layer has one responsibility, so a rule has one place to live and one place
to be tested.

### III. Strict TypeScript

- `interface` MUST NOT be used; use `class` for DTOs and `type` for everything else.
- `any` MUST NOT be used.
- An inline object type MUST NOT be used as a function parameter; define a named DTO class.
- Every repository method MUST have an explicit return type.
- Imports MUST be named imports; `import * as` MUST NOT be used.

Rationale: explicit, named types keep the contract visible at every boundary and stop
untyped data from leaking between layers.

### IV. Small, Self-Describing Files

- File names MUST be kebab-case and describe their purpose.
- Every code file MUST stay under 200 lines; split by concern.
- Comments MUST NOT restate what the code does. A comment is allowed only for a non-obvious
  constraint, in one short line.

Rationale: a file whose name and size reveal its purpose can be found and understood without
opening its neighbours.

### V. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

- Every new or modified service MUST have at least one unit test in a `*.spec.ts` file next
  to it.
- The failing test MUST be written before the implementation.

Rationale: a test written first proves the behaviour was missing and that the change added it.

## Safety Constraints

- `.env` and `.env.*` files MUST NOT be read; refer to configuration by variable name.
- Git is local only: no remote, no push, no pull request.
- Dependencies MUST NOT be added.

## Quality Gates

A change is finished only when all three commands pass:

- `pnpm run build`
- `pnpm run lint`
- `pnpm run test`

## Governance

- This constitution supersedes any other practice in this repository. Where another document
  conflicts with it, the constitution wins.
- Amendments are made by editing this file through `/speckit-constitution`, with the change
  recorded in a local commit.
- Versions follow semantic versioning: MAJOR for removing or redefining a principle, MINOR for
  adding a principle or section or materially expanding guidance, PATCH for clarifications and
  wording.
- Every specification, plan, task list and implementation MUST be checked against these
  principles. A violation MUST be fixed, or justified in writing in the plan, before the
  change is considered finished.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-11-10 | **Last Amended**: 2026-11-10

# Contract: Bookings HTTP API (gateway) — changes for the overlap rule

This is a delta to `specs/001-room-bookings/contracts/gateway-http-api.md`. Routes, request shapes,
success answers and every existing error stay as described there. Only what is listed here changes.

## Shared contract (`libs/contract`)

One addition, and nothing else (FR-015):

```text
ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP = 'CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP'
```

## Overlap rejection

`ErrorResponseDto`, the same on both routes:

```json
{
  "statusCode": 409,
  "errorCode": "CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP",
  "message": "The room is already booked for that time"
}
```

The body does not name the booking or bookings in the way. Clients must rely on `statusCode` and
`errorCode`; the `message` is for people and its wording may change.

## POST `/api/bookings`

Added row:

| Status | `errorCode` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 409 | `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` | the span overlaps an existing booking of the same room |

- Checked last: an invalid key, an invalid body, a reused key, an unknown room and an in-progress
  key are answered as before, even when the span is also taken.
- Nothing is stored against the `Idempotency-Key`. The 001 sentence "Only a 201 is stored against
  the key. After any error answer the key can be used again." covers it unchanged.
- Sending the same key and body again while the conflict remains answers 409 again, without
  `Idempotency-Replayed`.
- A replay of an earlier 201 is answered from the stored response and is never checked for overlap.
- Two 409 codes now exist on this route. `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` means "the same request
  is still running, try again"; `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` means "choose another time".

## PATCH `/api/bookings/:id`

Added row:

| Status | `errorCode` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 409 | `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` | the booking's resulting span (sent times, stored values for the rest) overlaps another booking of the same room |

- Checked last: 400 and 404 are answered as before.
- A booking never conflicts with itself.
- A rejected update leaves the booking unchanged, as for every other rejection.

## Simultaneous requests

- Two overlapping creates for one room: exactly one 201 and one 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
- An update racing with a create or another update for one room: at most one of two changes that
  would overlap each other succeeds; the other gets the 409.
- Requests for different rooms, or for spans of one room that do not overlap, do not reject each
  other.

## Service messages (NATS)

Delta to `specs/001-room-bookings/contracts/service-messages.md`. Patterns and payloads are
unchanged.

| Pattern | Change |
|---|---|
| `booking:createBooking` | may reject with the overlap rejection above |
| `booking:updateBooking` | may reject with the overlap rejection above |

The gateway forwards the rejection as it forwards every other `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`.

## Unchanged

`GET /api/bookings`, `GET /api/bookings/:id`, `DELETE /api/bookings/:id`, `GET /api/rooms`,
`GET /api/health/<service>`, the `Idempotency-Key` and `Idempotency-Replayed` headers, the
confirmation queue and its job.

# Contract: Bookings Page (`apps/web`) — behaviour on an overlap rejection

This is a delta to `specs/001-room-bookings/contracts/bookings-page.md`. Regions, accessible names,
the service layer and the idempotency key rule stay as described there.

The page does not look at the error code. It shows the `message` of whatever `ApiError` the service
layer rejects with; an overlap rejection is `ApiError` with `statusCode` 409, `errorCode`
`CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and the API's message.

## Create form — `form` "New booking"

When `createBooking` rejects with the overlap `ApiError`:

| What | Expected |
|---|---|
| Message | an `alert` inside the form with the API's `message` |
| Fields | Room, Title, Organizer email, Start and End still hold what was typed |
| List | not reloaded |
| Next submit | a new `Idempotency-Key` (the API answered) |

When the next submit succeeds: the alert is gone, the form is cleared and the list is reloaded.

## Edit dialog — `dialog` "Edit booking"

When `updateBooking` rejects with the overlap `ApiError`:

| What | Expected |
|---|---|
| Message | an `alert` inside the dialog's form with the API's `message` |
| Dialog | stays open |
| Fields | Title, Start and End still hold what was typed |
| Table row | still shows the booking's stored values; the list is not reloaded |

When the next save succeeds: the dialog closes and the list is reloaded with the updated booking.

## Tests

Page tests mock `apps/web/src/services/booking.service.ts`, as today. Each row above is asserted

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Starts infra, runs migrations, builds and starts every app. Exits 0 once the gateway answers.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

[ -f .env ] || scripts/make-local-env.sh
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env
set +a

mkdir -p tmp/logs tmp/pids

docker compose up -d --wait
pnpm run migration:run
pnpm run build

export NODE_ENV=production

start_app() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  "$@" > "tmp/logs/${name}.log" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "tmp/pids/${name}.pid"
}

for app in room booking worker gateway; do
  start_app "$app" node "dist/apps/${app}/main.js"
done
start_app web pnpm nx serve web --prod --port "${WEB_PORT}"

health_url="http://localhost:${GATEWAY_PORT}/api/health/gateway"
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fs -o /dev/null "$health_url"; then
    echo "Stack is up: gateway on ${GATEWAY_PORT}, web on ${WEB_PORT}." >&2
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 1
done

echo "Gateway did not answer at ${health_url}; see tmp/logs/." >&2
exit 1
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Drops the local data and starts a fresh stack.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

scripts/stack-down.sh --volumes
scripts/stack-up.sh
# Local setup

Requirements: Node 22 or newer, pnpm, Docker.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run stack:up      # infra, migrations, build, all five apps
pnpm run stack:down    # stop apps and infra, keep the data
pnpm run stack:reset   # drop the data and start fresh
```

`stack:up` creates `.env` on first run through `scripts/make-local-env.sh`. The file holds throwaway local values, is gitignored and must never be committed. App logs go to `tmp/logs/`.

To run a second copy of the stack on the same machine, set `PORT_OFFSET` and `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` before the first `stack:up`.

## Environment variables

| Name | Used by |
|---|---|
| `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`, `PORT_OFFSET` | docker compose, `scripts/make-local-env.sh` |
| `NODE_ENV` | all apps. Not kept in `.env`, where it would leak into `next build`; `stack:up` sets `production` when it starts the apps |
| `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_DATABASE` | `booking`, `room`, migrations |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Starts infra, runs migrations, builds and starts every app. Exits 0 once the gateway answers.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

[ -f .env ] || scripts/make-local-env.sh
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. ./.env
set +a

mkdir -p tmp/logs tmp/pids

docker compose up -d --wait
pnpm run migration:run
pnpm run build

export NODE_ENV=production

start_app() {
  local name="$1"
  shift
  "$@" > "tmp/logs/${name}.log" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "tmp/pids/${name}.pid"
}

for app in room booking worker gateway; do
  start_app "$app" node "dist/apps/${app}/main.js"
done
start_app web pnpm nx serve web --prod --port "${WEB_PORT}"

health_url="http://localhost:${GATEWAY_PORT}/api/health/gateway"
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fs -o /dev/null "$health_url"; then
    echo "Stack is up: gateway on ${GATEWAY_PORT}, web on ${WEB_PORT}." >&2
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 1
done

echo "Gateway did not answer at ${health_url}; see tmp/logs/." >&2
exit 1

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run stack:up      # infra, migrations, build, all five apps
pnpm run stack:down    # stop apps and infra, keep the data
pnpm run stack:reset   # drop the data and start fresh
```

`stack:up` creates `.env` on first run through `scripts/make-local-env.sh`. The file holds throwaway local values, is gitignored and must never be committed. App logs go to `tmp/logs/`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Writes a local .env with throwaway values. Never commit the result.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ -f .env ] && [ "${1:-}" != "--force" ]; then
  echo ".env already exists; leaving it alone (pass --force to regenerate it)." >&2
  exit 0
fi

offset="${PORT_OFFSET:-0}"
project="${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-roombook}"
gateway_port=$((3100 + offset))
web_port=$((4200 + offset))

umask 077
cat > .env <<ENV
COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=${project}
PORT_OFFSET=${offset}
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=$((5432 + offset))
DB_USERNAME=roombook
DB_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -hex 12)
DB_DATABASE=roombook
REDIS_HOST=localhost
REDIS_PORT=$((6379 + offset))
NATS_PORT=$((4222 + offset))
NATS_URL=nats://localhost:$((4222 + offset))
GATEWAY_PORT=${gateway_port}
WEB_PORT=${web_port}
WEB_ORIGIN=http://localhost:${web_port}
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:${gateway_port}/api
ENV
echo "Wrote .env for project ${project} (port offset ${offset})." >&2
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stops the apps started by stack-up.sh and the compose services. Pass --volumes to drop the data.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ -d tmp/pids ]; then
  for pid_file in tmp/pids/*.pid; do
    [ -e "$pid_file" ] || continue
    pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
    kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$pid_file"
  done
fi

if [ -f .env ]; then
  if [ "${1:-}" = "--volumes" ]; then
    docker compose down --volumes
  else
    docker compose down
  fi
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quickstart scenario 5: 100 rounds of two overlapping creates for one room. Usage: race-create.sh <gateway-port>
set -uo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh" "$1"
ROOM_R=$(room 0)

day_of() {
  date -u -j -v+"$1"d -f '%Y-%m-%d' 2031-06-01 '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || date -u -d "2031-06-01 +$1 day" '+%Y-%m-%d'
}

for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  DAY=$(day_of "$i")
  ( book "$ROOM_R" "${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z" & \
    book "$ROOM_R" "${DAY}T10:30:00.000Z" "${DAY}T11:30:00.000Z" & wait ) |
    awk '{print $1}' | sort | tr '\n' ' '
  echo
done | sort | uniq -c

echo "bookings for the room: $(curl -s "$API/bookings?roomId=$ROOM_R&limit=100" | jq '.total')"

# Scenario 4 uses its own day instead of a second reset.
set -uo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh" "$1"
R=$(room 0)
S=$(room 1)
OVERLAP='409 CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP'
t() { echo "2031-03-03T$1:00.000Z"; }
u() { echo "2031-03-04T$1:00.000Z"; }

body() {
  jq -nc --arg r "$1" --arg s "$2" --arg e "$3" \
    '{roomId:$r,title:"Overlap check",organizerEmail:"qa.user+overlap@example.com",startsAt:$s,endsAt:$e}'
}

# raw <json> [key] -> "<status> <errorCode|id>"
raw() {
  local args=(-s -w '\n%{http_code}' -X POST "$API/bookings" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$1")
  [ -n "${2:-}" ] && args+=(-H "Idempotency-Key: $2")
  curl "${args[@]}" | jq -rs '"\(.[1]) \(.[0].errorCode // .[0].id)"'
}

echo '--- 1. create'
A=$(book "$R" "$(t 10:00)" "$(t 11:00)")
expect 'R 10:00-11:00' "$A" 201
A_ID=$(detail_of "$A")
while read -r from to; do
  expect "R $from-$to" "$(book "$R" "$(t "$from")" "$(t "$to")")" "$OVERLAP"
done <<'SPANS'
10:30 11:30
10:00 11:00
10:15 10:45
09:00 12:00
SPANS
expect 'R 10:59:59.999-12:00' "$(book "$R" 2031-03-03T10:59:59.999Z "$(t 12:00)")" "$OVERLAP"
expect 'R 11:00-12:00 (touching)' "$(book "$R" "$(t 11:00)" "$(t 12:00)")" 201
expect 'R 09:00-10:00 (touching)' "$(book "$R" "$(t 09:00)" "$(t 10:00)")" 201
expect 'S 10:00-11:00 (other room)' "$(book "$S" "$(t 10:00)" "$(t 11:00)")" 201
expect 'DELETE A' "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X DELETE "$API/bookings/$A_ID")" 2
expect 'R 10:00-11:00 after the delete' "$(book "$R" "$(t 10:00)" "$(t 11:00)")" 201

echo '--- 2. order of checks'
TAKEN=$(body "$R" "$(t 10:00)" "$(t 11:00)")
expect 'no Idempotency-Key' "$(raw "$TAKEN")" '400 BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY'
expect 'title removed' "$(raw "$(echo "$TAKEN" | jq -c 'del(.title)')" "$(uuidgen)")" '400 BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION'
expect 'endsAt equal to startsAt' "$(book "$R" "$(t 10:00)" "$(t 10:00)")" '400 BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION'
UNKNOWN_ROOM=$(uuidgen | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
expect 'unknown room' "$(book "$UNKNOWN_ROOM" "$(t 10:00)" "$(t 11:00)")" '404 NOT_FOUND.ROOM'

echo '--- 3. a rejected create and its key'
KEY=$(uuidgen)
expect 'key, taken span' "$(book "$R" "$(t 10:30)" "$(t 11:30)" "$KEY")" "$OVERLAP"
expect 'same key and body again' "$(book "$R" "$(t 10:30)" "$(t 11:30)" "$KEY")" "$OVERLAP"
FIRST=$(book "$R" "$(t 14:00)" "$(t 15:00)" "$KEY")
expect 'same key, free span' "$FIRST" 201
expect 'same key and body replayed' "$(book "$R" "$(t 14:00)" "$(t 15:00)" "$KEY")" "$FIRST"

echo '--- 4. update'
A_ID=$(detail_of "$(book "$R" "$(u 10:00)" "$(u 11:00)")")
B_ID=$(detail_of "$(book "$R" "$(u 12:00)" "$(u 13:00)")")
C_ID=$(detail_of "$(book "$S" "$(u 10:00)" "$(u 11:00)")")
starts_at() { curl -s "$API/bookings/$1" | jq -r '.startsAt'; }
expect 'B start 10:30' "$(patch "$B_ID" "{\"startsAt\":\"$(u 10:30)\"}")" "$OVERLAP"
expect 'B unchanged' "$(starts_at "$B_ID")" "$(u 12:00)"
expect 'A end 12:30' "$(patch "$A_ID" "{\"endsAt\":\"$(u 12:30)\"}")" "$OVERLAP"
expect 'A end 12:00 (touching)' "$(patch "$A_ID" "{\"endsAt\":\"$(u 12:00)\"}")" 200
expect 'A title only' "$(patch "$A_ID" '{"title":"Renamed"}')" 200
expect 'A inside its own span' "$(patch "$A_ID" "{\"startsAt\":\"$(u 10:15)\",\"endsAt\":\"$(u 10:45)\"}")" 200
expect 'A over its previous span' "$(patch "$A_ID" "{\"startsAt\":\"$(u 10:30)\",\"endsAt\":\"$(u 11:30)\"}")" 200
expect 'A empty body' "$(patch "$A_ID" '{}')" 200
expect 'C to 12:00-13:00 in room S' "$(patch "$C_ID" "{\"startsAt\":\"$(u 12:00)\",\"endsAt\":\"$(u 13:00)\"}")" 200
expect 'B end 11:00 (invalid pair wins)' "$(patch "$B_ID" "{\"endsAt\":\"$(u 11:00)\"}")" '400 BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION'
expect 'unknown booking' "$(patch "$UNKNOWN_ROOM" "{\"startsAt\":\"$(u 10:30)\"}")" '404 NOT_FOUND.BOOKING'

finish

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quickstart scenario 5 variations and scenario 6. Usage: race-variations.sh <gateway-port>
# Every round uses its own day, so no state has to be restored between rounds.
set -uo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh" "$1"
R=$(room 0)
S=$(room 1)

day_of() {
  date -u -j -v+"$1"d -f '%Y-%m-%d' 2032-01-01 '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || date -u -d "2032-01-01 +$1 day" '+%Y-%m-%d'
}

echo '--- two rooms, same span: expected only "201 201"'
for i in $(seq 1 5); do
  DAY=$(day_of "$i")
  ( book "$R" "${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z" & \
    book "$S" "${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z" & wait ) | awk '{print $1}' | sort | tr '\n' ' '
  echo
done | sort | uniq -c

echo '--- one room, touching spans: expected only "201 201"'
for i in $(seq 11 15); do
  DAY=$(day_of "$i")
  ( book "$R" "${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z" & \
    book "$R" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T12:00:00.000Z" & wait ) | awk '{print $1}' | sort | tr '\n' ' '
  echo
done | sort | uniq -c

echo '--- same key and body twice: expected "201 201" or "201 409:CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS", never BOOKING_OVERLAP'
for i in $(seq 21 25); do
  DAY=$(day_of "$i")
  KEY=$(uuidgen)
  ( book "$R" "${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z" "$KEY" & \
    book "$R" "${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z" "$KEY" & wait ) |
    awk '{print ($1 == "201" ? $1 : $1 ":" $2)}' | sort | tr '\n' ' '
  echo "bookings that day: $(curl -s "$API/bookings?roomId=$R&limit=100" | jq --arg d "$DAY" '[.items[] | select(.startsAt | startswith($d))] | length')"
done | sort | uniq -c

echo '--- 6. update racing with a create: expected only "create=201 patch=409:CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP" or "create=409:CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP patch=200"'
for i in $(seq 31 50); do
  DAY=$(day_of "$i")
  A_ID=$(detail_of "$(book "$R" "${DAY}T10:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z")")
  ( echo "patch=$(patch "$A_ID" "{\"endsAt\":\"${DAY}T11:30:00.000Z\"}")" & \
    echo "create=$(book "$R" "${DAY}T11:00:00.000Z" "${DAY}T12:00:00.000Z")" & wait ) |
    awk '{split($1, part, "="); print part[1] "=" (part[2] ~ /^20/ ? part[2] : part[2] ":" $2)}' | sort | tr '\n' ' '
  echo
done | sort | uniq -c

description: "Task list for the No Overlapping Bookings feature"
---

# Tasks: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md

**Tests**: Included. FR-024 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: a spec task marked "failing" is done first and MUST fail (a compile error on a missing export counts) before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates, edits or runs

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/contract/src/lib/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/web/src/views/bookings/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- The only change to `libs/contract` is T002 (FR-015). Nothing is changed in `apps/room`, `apps/gateway`, `apps/worker`, `libs/backend-common`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `apps/web/src/services`, `package.json` or `specs/001-room-bookings` (FR-021, FR-022). No table, migration, route, message pattern or dependency is added.
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value from `@roombook/contract`.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method and query function, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. `.env` files are never read; configuration is referred to by variable name. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. **Spec files and the 200-line limit.** plan.md lists the existing specs as "edit", but four of them are within 25 lines of the limit. New cases therefore go to a new sibling file where the existing one would pass 200 lines: `idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts`, `booking.repository.update.spec.ts`, `booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx` and `bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx`. `create-booking.service.spec.ts`, `booking.service.spec.ts` and `booking-edit-dialog.spec.tsx` are edited in place; if one of them would reach 200 lines, its new cases move to a sibling `<name>.overlap.spec.ts(x)` instead.
2. **Names the design leaves open.** The two query functions are `lockRoom` and `isRoomSpanTaken`; the error function is `raiseBookingOverlap`; the new repository method is `BookingRepository.update`; the update result holds a `BookingEntity | null`.
3. **Repository specs mock `./booking-overlap.query`** with `jest.mock`, so the SQL text of the lock and the check is asserted once, in `booking-overlap.query.spec.ts`.
4. **User Story 3 adds no code.** The room lock is part of the create and update transactions built in User Stories 1 and 2 (plan.md, research R1); taking it out of them to add it later would leave those stories half-built. The unit tests that pin the lock and the order of statements are in those stories; the User Story 3 phase is the proof of the race against the running stack (research R7).
5. **User Story 4 specs are expected to pass when first run** (research R6): the page already has the behaviour. They are regression tests for the new error; a component is edited only if one of them fails.
6. `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `update-booking-result.dto.ts` hold no logic and get no spec of their own (plan.md).
7. T008 and T014 change existing specs so they keep passing with the new collaborators; they are not failing-first tasks.

---

## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)

**Purpose**: Confirm the starting point; the project, tooling and dependencies already exist.

- [ ] T001 Run `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` from the repository root (scripts in `package.json`) and confirm all three pass before any change; stop and report if one fails

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The one contract change and the two shared pieces both write paths use: the room lock with the overlap check, and the overlap rejection.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T002 Edit `libs/contract/src/lib/error-code.enum.ts`: add the member `BOOKING_OVERLAP = 'CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP'` on the line after `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`; change nothing else in `libs/contract`
- [ ] T003 [P] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.query.spec.ts` with an `EntityManager` whose `query` is a `jest.fn()`: `lockRoom(manager, roomId)` runs exactly one statement, `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0))`, with the parameters `['room:<roomId>']`, and two different room ids give two different lock names; `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, roomId, startsAt, endsAt, excludedBookingId)` runs exactly one statement whose text contains `"room_id" = $1`, `"starts_at" < $3`, `"ends_at" > $2` and `$4::uuid IS NULL OR "id" <> $4::uuid` and does not contain `confirmation_status`, with the parameters `[roomId, startsAt, endsAt, excludedBookingId]` (`null` passed through as `null`), and returns `true` for the row `[{ taken: true }]` and `false` for `[{ taken: false }]`
- [ ] T004 [P] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.error.spec.ts` (after T002): `raiseBookingOverlap()` throws an `RpcException` whose error is exactly `{ statusCode: 409, errorCode: ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP, message: 'The room is already booked for that time' }` (read the error the way the `errorOf` helper of `create-booking.service.spec.ts` does)
- [ ] T005 [P] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.query.ts` exporting `lockRoom(manager: EntityManager, roomId: string): Promise<void>` (kind: transaction-scoped advisory lock, waiting (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`); name: `room:<roomId>`, hashed with `hashtextextended(…, 0)`) and `isRoomSpanTaken(manager: EntityManager, roomId: string, startsAt: Date, endsAt: Date, excludedBookingId: string | null): Promise<boolean>` (`SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "bookings" WHERE "room_id" = $1 AND "starts_at" < $3 AND "ends_at" > $2 AND ($4::uuid IS NULL OR "id" <> $4::uuid)) AS "taken"`): a stored booking `b` is in the way when `b.room_id = R AND b.starts_at < end AND b.ends_at > start`, and, on update, `b.id` is not the booking being changed; both are plain functions, not providers (T003 passes)
- [ ] T006 [P] Create `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.error.ts` exporting `raiseBookingOverlap(): never`, one statement: `ExceptionHelper.conflict(ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP, 'The room is already booked for that time')` (T004 passes; depends on T002)

**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run build` and `pnpm run test` pass; user story work can begin.

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 - A room cannot be double-booked on create (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: `POST /api/bookings` for a span that overlaps a booking of the same room is answered 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; nothing is stored against the booking, the `Idempotency-Key` or the queue. Touching spans and other rooms are still accepted.

**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create a booking for a room, then send creates for the same room that overlap it, touch it and sit in another room, and reuse the key of a rejected create (quickstart scenarios 1, 2 and 3).

### Tests for User Story 1 (write first, must fail) ⚠️

- [ ] T007 [P] [US1] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts` with the `DataSource`, query runner and `manager` mocked as in `idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts` and `./booking-overlap.query` mocked with `jest.mock`: (a) free span — `claim` calls `lockRoom(manager, booking.roomId)` then `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, booking.roomId, new Date(booking.startsAt), new Date(booking.endsAt), null)`, in this order by `invocationCallOrder`: `manager.findOneBy` (stored key) → `lockRoom` → `isRoomSpanTaken` → `manager.save`, and answers `CREATED`; (b) `isRoomSpanTaken` resolves `true` — the result is `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }`, `manager.save` and `manager.insert` are not called, the transaction is committed once, not rolled back, and the runner released once; (c) for each of `IN_PROGRESS` (first try-lock not obtained), `KEY_REUSED` (second try-lock not obtained), `REPLAYED` (stored row, same fingerprint) and `KEY_REUSED` (stored row, other fingerprint) neither `lockRoom` nor `isRoomSpanTaken` is called
- [ ] T008 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts`: add `jest.mock('./booking-overlap.query')` and, in `beforeEach`, make `isRoomSpanTaken` resolve `false` and `lockRoom` resolve; change no existing case and keep the file under 200 lines
- [ ] T009 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.spec.ts`: in `claim outcomes` add a failing case — a claim `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }` raises 409 with `errorCode` `ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and the message `The room is already booked for that time`, and `ConfirmationQueueProducer.enqueue` is not called; in `the same key after a rejected request` add a failing case — after an `OVERLAP` claim, the same key and body with the claim still `OVERLAP` raises the same 409 again (not a replay), and the same key with a claim that answers `CREATED` returns `{ booking, replayed: false }` and enqueues exactly one job

### Implementation for User Story 1

- [ ] T010 [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/claim-booking-result.dto.ts`: add `OVERLAP = 'OVERLAP'` to `ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum` after `IN_PROGRESS`
- [ ] T011 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/idempotent-booking.repository.ts`: in `claimWithin`, after the stored-key branch and before `insertBookingWithKey`, call `lockRoom(manager, booking.roomId)`, then `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, booking.roomId, new Date(booking.startsAt), new Date(booking.endsAt), null)`, and return `{ outcome: ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP, booking: null }` when it is `true`; the order inside the transaction is: try-lock key+fingerprint → try-lock key → read stored key → lock room (waits) → overlap check → insert booking + idempotency row (T007 passes, T008 stays green; depends on T005, T010)
- [ ] T012 [P] [US1] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/create-booking.service.ts`: in `toResult`, after the `IN_PROGRESS` branch, call `raiseBookingOverlap()` when the outcome is `ClaimBookingOutcomeEnum.OVERLAP`; the enqueue stays limited to outcome `CREATED` and the order of the earlier checks (stored key, time pair, room) is not changed (T009 passes; depends on T006, T010)

**Checkpoint**: `pnpm run test` passes; quickstart scenarios 1, 2 and 3 pass against the running stack.

---

## Phase 4: User Story 2 - A room cannot be double-booked by moving a booking (Priority: P2)

**Goal**: `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` whose resulting span overlaps another booking of the same room is answered 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and leaves the booking unchanged; 404 and 400 are answered as before and win over overlap; a booking never conflicts with itself.

**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create two bookings of one room that do not overlap, then update one with times that overlap the other, touch the other and stay within its own span (quickstart scenario 4).

### Tests for User Story 2 (write first, must fail) ⚠️

- [ ] T013 [P] [US2] Write the failing spec `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.update.spec.ts` for `BookingRepository.update(id, changes)`, with the `BookingEntity` repository token mocked, the `DataSource` mocked as a query runner whose `manager` has `findOneBy` and `query` (pattern of `idempotent-booking.repository.spec.ts`), and `./booking-overlap.query` mocked; the stored booking is 09:00–10:00 in room `R`: (a) first read finds no row → `{ outcome: NOT_FOUND, booking: null }`, `lockRoom` not called; (b) the read after the lock finds no row → `NOT_FOUND`; (c) `{ endsAt: 09:00 }` and `{ startsAt: 10:30 }` → `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` (resulting `ends_at` not later than resulting `starts_at`; the stored value is used for the time that was not sent), `isRoomSpanTaken` not called; (d) `isRoomSpanTaken` resolves `true` → `OVERLAP` with `booking: null` and no `UPDATE`; (e) `{ endsAt: 11:00 }` → `isRoomSpanTaken(manager, R, stored start, 11:00, id)` and one `UPDATE "bookings"` whose text still contains `"title" = COALESCE($2::varchar, "title")`, `"starts_at" = COALESCE($3::timestamptz, "starts_at")`, `"ends_at" = COALESCE($4::timestamptz, "ends_at")`, `"updated_at" = now()`, `COALESCE($4::timestamptz, "ends_at") > COALESCE($3::timestamptz, "starts_at")` and `RETURNING`, with the parameters `[id, null, null, new Date(11:00)]`, answering `{ outcome: UPDATED, booking: <returned row> }`; (f) a title-only change takes the lock and checks the stored span; (g) the `UPDATE` returns no row → `NOT_FOUND`; (h) order by `invocationCallOrder`: first read → `lockRoom(manager, R)` → second read → `isRoomSpanTaken` → `UPDATE`; (i) every outcome commits once and releases once; a statement that rejects rolls back, releases and rethrows
- [ ] T014 [P] [US2] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.repository.spec.ts`: remove the `updateIfTimeRangeValid` describe (its SQL assertions now live in T013) and add `{ provide: DataSource, useValue: { createQueryRunner: jest.fn() } }` to the providers; change no other case
- [ ] T015 [P] [US2] Edit `apps/booking/src/booking/booking.service.spec.ts`: mock `BookingRepository.update` in place of `updateIfTimeRangeValid` and replace the three cases that follow the repository update with four failing ones — `UPDATED` returns the mapped DTO; `NOT_FOUND` raises 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` (`Booking not found`); `INVALID_TIME_RANGE` raises 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` (`endsAt must be later than startsAt`); `OVERLAP` raises 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` (`The room is already booked for that time`) — and in all four `findById` is not called; the no-field case (stored booking returned, `update` not called) and the unparsable-time case (400, `update` not called) stay as they are

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: no dependencies.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: after Setup; blocks every user story. T002 → T004 → T006; T003 → T005.
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: after Foundational.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: after Foundational; shares no file with User Story 1.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: T019 and T020 after User Story 1; T021 after User Stories 1 and 2.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: after T002 only (its mocks use `ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP`); shares no file with the backend stories.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: after every story.

### User Story Dependencies

```text
Setup → Foundational ─┬─▶ US1 (create) ──┬─▶ US3 (race proof: T019, T020)
                      │                  └─▶ ┐
                      ├─▶ US2 (update) ──────┴─▶ US3 (T021)
                      └─▶ US4 (page tests)
                                   all ─▶ Polish
```

- **US1 (P1)**: independent; the MVP.
- **US2 (P2)**: independent of US1 in code; delivered second because it closes the bypass of US1.
- **US3 (P3)**: depends on US1 (and on US2 for T021); it proves, it does not build.
- **US4 (P4)**: independent in code; meaningful by hand (T030) only once US1 and US2 run.

### Within Each User Story

- Spec tasks first; a "failing" spec MUST fail before its implementation task starts.
- DTO (T010, T016) before the repository and the service that use it.
- Repository and service of one story are in different files and can be done in parallel once the DTO exists.
- Story complete, with its checkpoint, before the next priority.

### Parallel Opportunities

- Phase 2: T003 and T004 together; then T005 and T006 together.
- US1: T007, T008 and T009 together; after T010, T011 and T012 together.
- US2: T013, T014 and T015 together; after T016, T017 and T018 together.
- US4: T022, T023 and T024 together.
- After Foundational, US1, US2 and US4 can be worked on at the same time: they share no file.
- Polish: T027 and T028 together.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Phase 1: Setup (T001).
2. Phase 2: Foundational (T002–T006).
3. Phase 3: User Story 1 (T007–T012).
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: `pnpm run test`, then quickstart scenarios 1 to 3.

At this point a room can no longer be double-booked by a create, also under a race; it can still be double-booked by moving a booking until User Story 2 is done.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → the error code, the lock, the check and the rejection exist.
2. User Story 1 → create is safe (MVP).
3. User Story 2 → update is safe; the rule can no longer be bypassed.
4. User Story 3 → the race is proven against the running stack.
5. User Story 4 → the page behaviour is pinned by tests.
6. Polish → gates, scope check, full quickstart.

### Parallel Team Strategy

After Foundational, three people can take User Story 1, User Story 2 and User Story 4 at once; User Story 3 follows when 1 and 2 are merged.

# Tasks: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md

**Tests**: Included. FR-024 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: a spec task marked "failing" is done first and MUST fail (a compile error on a missing export counts) before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates, edits or runs

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/contract/src/lib/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/web/src/views/bookings/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- The only change to `libs/contract` is T002 (FR-015). Nothing is changed in `apps/room`, `apps/gateway`, `apps/worker`, `libs/backend-common`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `apps/web/src/services`, `package.json` or `specs/001-room-bookings` (FR-021, FR-022). No table, migration, route, message pattern or dependency is added.
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value from `@roombook/contract`.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method and query function, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. `.env` files are never read; configuration is referred to by variable name. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. **Spec files and the 200-line limit.** plan.md lists the existing specs as "edit", but four of them are within 25 lines of the limit. New cases therefore go to a new sibling file where the existing one would pass 200 lines: `idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts`, `booking.repository.update.spec.ts`, `booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx` and `bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx`. `create-booking.service.spec.ts`, `booking.service.spec.ts` and `booking-edit-dialog.spec.tsx` are edited in place; if one of them would reach 200 lines, its new cases move to a sibling `<name>.overlap.spec.ts(x)` instead.
2. **Names the design leaves open.** The two query functions are `lockRoom` and `isRoomSpanTaken`; the error function is `raiseBookingOverlap`; the new repository method is `BookingRepository.update`; the update result holds a `BookingEntity | null`.
3. **Repository specs mock `./booking-overlap.query`** with `jest.mock`, so the SQL text of the lock and the check is asserted once, in `booking-overlap.query.spec.ts`.
4. **User Story 3 adds no code.** The room lock is part of the create and update transactions built in User Stories 1 and 2 (plan.md, research R1); taking it out of them to add it later would leave those stories half-built. The unit tests that pin the lock and the order of statements are in those stories; the User Story 3 phase is the proof of the race against the running stack (research R7).
5. **User Story 4 specs are expected to pass when first run** (research R6): the page already has the behaviour. They are regression tests for the new error; a component is edited only if one of them fails.
6. `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `update-booking-result.dto.ts` hold no logic and get no spec of their own (plan.md).
7. T008 and T014 change existing specs so they keep passing with the new collaborators; they are not failing-first tasks.

**Purpose**: Confirm the starting point; the project, tooling and dependencies already exist.

- [X] T001 Run `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` from the repository root (scripts in `package.json`) and confirm all three pass before any change; stop and report if one fails

**Purpose**: The one contract change and the two shared pieces both write paths use: the room lock with the overlap check, and the overlap rejection.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: no dependencies.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: after Setup; blocks every user story. T002 → T004 → T006; T003 → T005.
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: after Foundational.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: after Foundational; shares no file with User Story 1.

- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: after T002 only (its mocks use `ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP`); shares no file with the backend stories.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: after every story.

### User Story Dependencies

```text
Setup → Foundational ─┬─▶ US1 (create) ──┬─▶ US3 (race proof: T019, T020)
                      │                  └─▶ ┐
                      ├─▶ US2 (update) ──────┴─▶ US3 (T021)
                      └─▶ US4 (page tests)
                                   all ─▶ Polish
```

- **US1 (P1)**: independent; the MVP.
- **US2 (P2)**: independent of US1 in code; delivered second because it closes the bypass of US1.

- US2: T013, T014 and T015 together; after T016, T017 and T018 together.

# Tasks: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md

**Tests**: Included. FR-024 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: a spec task marked "failing" is done first and MUST fail (a compile error on a missing export counts) before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates, edits or runs

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/contract/src/lib/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/web/src/views/bookings/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- The only change to `libs/contract` is T002 (FR-015). Nothing is changed in `apps/room`, `apps/gateway`, `apps/worker`, `libs/backend-common`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `apps/web/src/services`, `package.json` or `specs/001-room-bookings` (FR-021, FR-022). No table, migration, route, message pattern or dependency is added.
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value from `@roombook/contract`.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method and query function, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. `.env` files are never read; configuration is referred to by variable name. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. **Spec files and the 200-line limit.** plan.md lists the existing specs as "edit", but four of them are within 25 lines of the limit. New cases therefore go to a new sibling file where the existing one would pass 200 lines: `idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts`, `booking.repository.update.spec.ts`, `booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx` and `bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx`. `create-booking.service.spec.ts`, `booking.service.spec.ts` and `booking-edit-dialog.spec.tsx` are edited in place; if one of them would reach 200 lines, its new cases move to a sibling `<name>.overlap.spec.ts(x)` instead.
2. **Names the design leaves open.** The two query functions are `lockRoom` and `isRoomSpanTaken`; the error function is `raiseBookingOverlap`; the new repository method is `BookingRepository.update`; the update result holds a `BookingEntity | null`.
3. **Repository specs mock `./booking-overlap.query`** with `jest.mock`, so the SQL text of the lock and the check is asserted once, in `booking-overlap.query.spec.ts`.
4. **User Story 3 adds no code.** The room lock is part of the create and update transactions built in User Stories 1 and 2 (plan.md, research R1); taking it out of them to add it later would leave those stories half-built. The unit tests that pin the lock and the order of statements are in those stories; the User Story 3 phase is the proof of the race against the running stack (research R7).
5. **User Story 4 specs are expected to pass when first run** (research R6): the page already has the behaviour. They are regression tests for the new error; a component is edited only if one of them fails.
6. `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `update-booking-result.dto.ts` hold no logic and get no spec of their own (plan.md).
7. T008 and T014 change existing specs so they keep passing with the new collaborators; they are not failing-first tasks.

## Phase 3: User Story 1 - A room cannot be double-booked on create (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: `POST /api/bookings` for a span that overlaps a booking of the same room is answered 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`; nothing is stored against the booking, the `Idempotency-Key` or the queue. Touching spans and other rooms are still accepted.

**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create a booking for a room, then send creates for the same room that overlap it, touch it and sit in another room, and reuse the key of a rejected create (quickstart scenarios 1, 2 and 3).

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: no dependencies.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: after Setup; blocks every user story. T002 → T004 → T006; T003 → T005.
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: after Foundational.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: after Foundational; shares no file with User Story 1.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: T019 and T020 after User Story 1; T021 after User Stories 1 and 2.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: after T002 only (its mocks use `ErrorCodeEnum.BOOKING_OVERLAP`); shares no file with the backend stories.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: after every story.

### User Story Dependencies

```text
Setup → Foundational ─┬─▶ US1 (create) ──┬─▶ US3 (race proof: T019, T020)
                      │                  └─▶ ┐
                      ├─▶ US2 (update) ──────┴─▶ US3 (T021)
                      └─▶ US4 (page tests)
                                   all ─▶ Polish
```

- **US1 (P1)**: independent; the MVP.
- **US2 (P2)**: independent of US1 in code; delivered second because it closes the bypass of US1.
- **US3 (P3)**: depends on US1 (and on US2 for T021); it proves, it does not build.
- **US4 (P4)**: independent in code; meaningful by hand (T030) only once US1 and US2 run.

### Within Each User Story

- Spec tasks first; a "failing" spec MUST fail before its implementation task starts.
- DTO (T010, T016) before the repository and the service that use it.
- Repository and service of one story are in different files and can be done in parallel once the DTO exists.
- Story complete, with its checkpoint, before the next priority.

### Parallel Opportunities

- Phase 2: T003 and T004 together; then T005 and T006 together.
- US1: T007, T008 and T009 together; after T010, T011 and T012 together.
- US2: T013, T014 and T015 together; after T016, T017 and T018 together.
- US4: T022, T023 and T024 together.
- After Foundational, US1, US2 and US4 can be worked on at the same time: they share no file.
- Polish: T027 and T028 together.

# Tasks: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/`

**Tests**: Included. FR-024 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: a spec task marked "failing" is done first and MUST fail (a compile error on a missing export counts) before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates, edits or runs

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/contract/src/lib/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/web/src/views/bookings/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- The only change to `libs/contract` is T002 (FR-015). Nothing is changed in `apps/room`, `apps/gateway`, `apps/worker`, `libs/backend-common`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `apps/web/src/services`, `package.json` or `specs/001-room-bookings` (FR-021, FR-022). No table, migration, route, message pattern or dependency is added.
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value from `@roombook/contract`.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method and query function, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. `.env` files are never read; configuration is referred to by variable name. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. **Spec files and the 200-line limit.** plan.md lists the existing specs as "edit", but four of them are within 25 lines of the limit. New cases therefore go to a new sibling file where the existing one would pass 200 lines: `idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts`, `booking.repository.update.spec.ts`, `booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx` and `bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx`. `create-booking.service.spec.ts`, `booking.service.spec.ts` and `booking-edit-dialog.spec.tsx` are edited in place; if one of them would reach 200 lines, its new cases move to a sibling `<name>.overlap.spec.ts(x)` instead.
2. **Names the design leaves open.** The two query functions are `lockRoom` and `isRoomSpanTaken`; the error function is `raiseBookingOverlap`; the new repository method is `BookingRepository.update`; the update result holds a `BookingEntity | null`.
3. **Repository specs mock `./booking-overlap.query`** with `jest.mock`, so the SQL text of the lock and the check is asserted once, in `booking-overlap.query.spec.ts`.
4. **User Story 3 adds no code.** The room lock is part of the create and update transactions built in User Stories 1 and 2 (plan.md, research R1); taking it out of them to add it later would leave those stories half-built. The unit tests that pin the lock and the order of statements are in those stories; the User Story 3 phase is the proof of the race against the running stack (research R7).
5. **User Story 4 specs are expected to pass when first run** (research R6): the page already has the behaviour. They are regression tests for the new error; a component is edited only if one of them fails.
6. `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `update-booking-result.dto.ts` hold no logic and get no spec of their own (plan.md).
7. T008 and T014 change existing specs so they keep passing with the new collaborators; they are not failing-first tasks.

# Tasks: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md

**Tests**: Included. FR-024 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: a spec task marked "failing" is done first and MUST fail (a compile error on a missing export counts) before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates, edits or runs

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/contract/src/lib/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/web/src/views/bookings/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- The only change to `libs/contract` is T002 (FR-015). Nothing is changed in `apps/room`, `apps/gateway`, `apps/worker`, `libs/backend-common`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `apps/web/src/services`, `package.json` or `specs/001-room-bookings` (FR-021, FR-022). No table, migration, route, message pattern or dependency is added.
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value from `@roombook/contract`.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method and query function, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. `.env` files are never read; configuration is referred to by variable name. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. **Spec files and the 200-line limit.** plan.md lists the existing specs as "edit", but four of them are within 25 lines of the limit. 4. **User Story 3 adds no code.** The room lock is part of the create and update transactions built in User Stories 1 and 2 (plan.md, research R1); taking it out of them to add it later would leave those stories half-built. The unit tests that pin the lock and the order of statements are in those stories; the User Story 3 phase is the proof of the race against the running stack (research R7).
5. **User Story 4 specs are expected to pass when first run** (research R6): the page already has the behaviour. They are regression tests for the new error; a component is edited only if one of them fails.
6. `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `update-booking-result.dto.ts` hold no logic and get no spec of their own (plan.md).
7. T008 and T014 change existing specs so they keep passing with the new collaborators; they are not failing-first tasks.

# Tasks: No Overlapping Bookings for the Same Room

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-prevent-booking-overlap/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/ (gateway-http-api.md, bookings-page.md), quickstart.md

**Tests**: Included. FR-024 and Constitution Principle V (Test-First, non-negotiable) require them: a spec task marked "failing" is done first and MUST fail (a compile error on a missing export counts) before the implementation task that follows it.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story so each story can be implemented and tested on its own.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependency on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1–US4)
- Every task names the exact file it creates, edits or runs

## Path Conventions

Nx monorepo, paths from the repository root: `libs/contract/src/lib/…`, `apps/booking/src/booking/…`, `apps/web/src/views/bookings/…`. A spec sits next to its source file as `*.spec.ts` / `*.spec.tsx`.

## Rules that apply to every task

- The only change to `libs/contract` is T002 (FR-015). Nothing is changed in `apps/room`, `apps/gateway`, `apps/worker`, `libs/backend-common`, `apps/web/src/views/rooms`, `apps/web/src/pages`, `apps/web/src/services`, `package.json` or `specs/001-room-bookings` (FR-021, FR-022). No table, migration, route, message pattern or dependency is added.
- Errors are raised with `ExceptionHelper` from `@roombook/backend-common` and an `ErrorCodeEnum` value from `@roombook/contract`.
- No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object type as a parameter, explicit return type on every repository method and query function, named imports only, kebab-case file names, every file under 200 lines, no narrative comments.
- Transactions only in repositories. `.env` files are never read; configuration is referred to by variable name. Git stays local.

## Assumptions made in this task list

1. **Spec files and the 200-line limit.** plan.md lists the existing specs as "edit", but four of them are within 25 lines of the limit. New cases therefore go to a new sibling file where the existing one would pass 200 lines: `idempotent-booking.repository.overlap.spec.ts`, `booking.repository.update.spec.ts`, `booking-create-form.overlap.spec.tsx` and `bookings-page.overlap.spec.tsx`. `create-booking.service.spec.ts`, `booking.service.spec.ts` and `booking-edit-dialog.spec.tsx` are edited in place; if one of them would reach 200 lines, its new cases move to a sibling `<name>.overlap.spec.ts(x)` instead.
2. **Names the design leaves open.** The two query functions are `lockRoom` and `isRoomSpanTaken`; the error function is `raiseBookingOverlap`; the new repository method is `BookingRepository.update`; the update result holds a `BookingEntity | null`.
3. **Repository specs mock `./booking-overlap.query`** with `jest.mock`, so the SQL text of the lock and the check is asserted once, in `booking-overlap.query.spec.ts`.
4. **User Story 3 adds no code.** The room lock is part of the create and update transactions built in User Stories 1 and 2 (plan.md, research R1); taking it out of them to add it later would leave those stories half-built. The unit tests that pin the lock and the order of statements are in those stories; the User Story 3 phase is the proof of the race against the running stack (research R7).
5. **User Story 4 specs are expected to pass when first run** (research R6): the page already has the behaviour. They are regression tests for the new error; a component is edited only if one of them fails.
6. `claim-booking-result.dto.ts` and `update-booking-result.dto.ts` hold no logic and get no spec of their own (plan.md).
7. T008 and T014 change existing specs so they keep passing with the new collaborators; they are not failing-first tasks.


- Phase 2: T003 and T004 together; then T005 and T006 together.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Phase 1: Setup (T001).
2. Phase 2: Foundational (T002–T006).
3. Phase 3: User Story 1 (T007–T012).
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: `pnpm run test`, then quickstart scenarios 1 to 3.

At this point a room can no longer be double-booked by a create, also under a race; it can still be double-booked by moving a booking until User Story 2 is done.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → the error code, the lock, the check and the rejection exist.
2. User Story 1 → create is safe (MVP).
3. User Story 2 → update is safe; the rule can no longer be bypassed.
4. User Story 3 → the race is proven against the running stack.
5. User Story 4 → the page behaviour is pinned by tests.
6. Polish → gates, scope check, full quickstart.

### Parallel Team Strategy

The overlap rule is implemented and 25 of 30 tasks are done, but the five tasks that prove it against the running stack were not run. `curl` and ad-hoc scripts are outside this session's allowed commands, so the race (SC-003) is covered only by unit tests with the database mocked.

### What was built
- **Contract**: `BOOKING_OVERLAP = 'CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP'` added to `ErrorCodeEnum`; it is the only change in `libs/contract`.
